title: feat(ui/tabs): [IPERIA-8546] add generic Tabs component using base-ui and implement it in TrainingAgency component
description:
## Tabs component & TrainingAgency labeling tabs
                                                                                                                                 
  ### Summary
                                                                                                                                 
  - Add a generic, reusable `Tabs` component (`ui/tabs`) built on top of `@base-ui/react/tabs`, with a compositional API.
  - Replace the legacy border-triangle hack with a `clip-path`-based slanted tab style — cleaner DOM and no extra pseudo-element 
  trickery.
  - Align `CardTabs` / `CardTabItems` on the new `Tabs__*` class names and ARIA roles (`tablist`, `tab`, `aria-selected`) so the 
  legacy in-card tabs share the same look & a11y.                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  - Extract the labelisation UI + edit modal into a dedicated `LabelisationSection` component so each tab owns its own state/modal.                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - Drive-by: rename `TooltipPrimitive` → `BaseTooltip` (IPERIA-8533 follow-up) for consistency with the base-ui naming used
  elsewhere. 
  - Use the new component on the **TrainingAgency** page to split the labelisation block into 3 tabs:
    - `APPEL D'OFFRES` (existing behavior: CALL_FOR_TENDER)                                                                                       
    - `MARCHÉ PUBLIC - LOT 1` (PM_BUNDLE_1)                                                                                
    - `MARCHÉ PUBLIC - LOT 2` (PM_BUNDLE_2)    


| Example1 | Example2 |

title: feat(ModulePathForm): [IPERIA-8554] check labeling eligibility against different MarketSegments
description:
Rework `ModulePathForm` to verify, on every relevant change, whether the training agency holds an
  eligible labeling for the selected **market segment**, **period** and **territory** — and surface
  the outcome through contextual banners.

  ### Changes

  - **Banners orchestration** — add `LabelingEligibilityBannerMessage` orchestrating
  `SingleOptionInfoBanner`, `InvalidWithReasonsBanner`, `FullyInvalidBanner` and
  `TechnicalErrorBanner`.
  - **Eligibility check** — add `useCheckModulePathLabelingEligibility` (TanStack Query) with
  debounced input via `useDebouncedValue`, MSW handlers and eligibility mocks.
  - **Helpers** — add `labelingEligibilityHelpers` (`isFullyIneligible`,
  `getExactlyOneAllowedLabeling`) + unit tests.
  - **UI** — add `DepartmentsList` and the `LabelingEligibilityDTO` model.
  - **TrainingMode** — adjust `TrainingMode` helpers, `TrainingModeMomentsForm` and related tests to
   fit the new MarketSegment-aware flow.





Closes IPERIA-8554
commits: feat(ModulePathForm): [IPERIA-8554] check labeling eligibility against different MarketSegment

+

+

+- Use plain Vitest (`*.test.ts`) for pure functions and utilities only
+- Test user interactions and behaviour, not implementation details
+- Refer to `agent-os/standards/testing/test-writing.md` for detailed patterns
+
+## Accessibility
+
+- Use semantic HTML elements
+- Implement proper ARIA attributes when needed
+- Handle focus management in dynamic content
+- Test with screen readers

+## Core principles
 
-For details, refer to the information provided in this file:

+- **Test only core user flows**: critical paths and primary workflows first; skip non-critical utilities
+- **Defer edge cases**: unless business-critical, address in dedicated testing phases
+- **Write minimal tests during development**: complete the feature first, then add tests at logical completion points
+- **Clear test names**: describe what is tested and the expected outcome
+- **Fast execution**: keep unit tests in milliseconds so they run frequently
+
+---
+
+## Unit tests (non-browser)
+
+Unit tests run in Node — no browser, no DOM. Use them exclusively for pure functions and utilities.
+
+### Imports
+
+```ts
+import { describe, it, test, expect, vi, beforeAll, afterAll, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
+```
+
+### Pure functions
+
+```ts
+describe('pluralize()', () => {
+  it('returns singular when count is 1', () => {
+    expect(pluralize(1, 'évaluation')).toBe('1 évaluation');
+  });
+
+  it('returns plural when count > 1', () => {
+    expect(pluralize(2, 'évaluation')).toBe('2 évaluations');
+  });
+});
+```
+
+### Mocking
+
+```ts
+// Function mock
+const onClose = vi.fn();
+
+// Spy on a module export
+const spy = vi.spyOn(myModule, 'someFunction');
+expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedArg);
+
+// Mock global / Date
+beforeAll(() => {
+  Date.now = vi.fn(() => new Date('2024-01-01').valueOf());
+});
+afterAll(() => {
+  global.Date.now = realNow;
+});
+
+// Reset between tests
+beforeEach(() => {
+  vi.clearAllMocks();
+});
+```
+
+### Assertions
+
+```ts
+expect(result).toBe(10);
+expect(result).toEqual({ key: 'value' });
+expect(result).toBeCloseTo(7.65);
+expect(result).toBeTruthy();
+expect(result).toBeNull();
+
+expect(mockFn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedArg);
+expect(mockFn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+```
+
+---
+
+## Component / Integration tests (browser)
+
+These tests run in a real browser (Chromium via Playwright). Use them for anything involving React components, user interactions, form behaviour, or API calls.
+
+- **File naming**: `*.browser.test.tsx`
+- **Render helper**: `renderWithProviders` from `@/test/browser-test-utils/renderWithProviders`
+- **Test runner**: `test` for no API, `testMsw` for API mocking (MSW worker auto-managed)
+- **Queries**: `page` locator from `vitest/browser` — prefer `getByRole`
+- **Assertions**: `await expect.element(locator).*`
+- **Interactions**: `locator.click()`, `locator.fill()`, `userEvent.keyboard()`
+
+---
+
+## File conventions
+
+- Browser integration tests: `*.browser.test.tsx`
+- Unit / helper tests: `*.test.ts` (no browser needed)
+- Location: `src/**/__tests__/ComponentName.browser.test.tsx`
+
+---
+
+## Imports
+
+```ts
+import { describe, expect, vi, test } from 'vitest';
+import { page, userEvent } from 'vitest/browser';
+import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
+
+import { renderWithProviders } from '@/test/browser-test-utils/renderWithProviders';
+import { testMsw } from '@/test/browser-test-utils/test-extend';
+```
+
+---
+
+## `test` vs `testMsw`
+
+|           | `test`           | `testMsw`                           |
+| --------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- |
+| Use when  | No API calls     | Component makes API calls           |
+| Worker    | None             | Auto-started, reset after each test |
+| Signature | `async () => {}` | `async ({ worker }) => {}`          |
+
+```ts
+// No API — use test
+test('should render correctly', async () => {
+  await renderComponent();
+});
+
+// Has API — use testMsw
+testMsw('should submit form', async ({ worker }) => {
+  worker.use(
+    http.put(endpoints.someEndpoint('id'), () => HttpResponse.json(null, { status: 200 })),
+  );
+  await renderComponent();
+});
+```
+
+Optionally set timeout when the test loads async data:
+
+```ts
+testMsw('should load data', { timeout: 30000 }, async ({ worker }) => { ... });
+```
+
+---
+
+## `renderWithProviders`
+
+```ts
+await renderWithProviders(<MyComponent />, {
+  preloadedState?: Partial<RootState>,   // Redux initial state
+  pathname?: string,                     // Current route (default: '/')
+  initialEntries?: string[],             // Router history entries
+  withQueryClient?: boolean,             // true when component uses TanStack Query
+  withRouter?: boolean,                  // false to disable router wrapper
+  useReducerGenerator?: boolean,         // true for legacy reducer-generated reducers
+});
+```
+
+Typical pattern — define once, reuse across tests:
+
+```ts
+function renderComponent(props = defaultProps) {
+  return renderWithProviders(
+    <MyForm {...props} />,
+    { withQueryClient: true, withRouter: false },
+  );
+}
+```
+
+---
+
+## Querying elements
+
+Prefer `getByRole` with accessible name. Fall back to `getByText` only for non-interactive content.
+
+```ts
+// Roles
+page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i });
+page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }); // matches "Date début*" too (substring)
+page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Statut' });
+page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Présentiel' });
+page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Présentiel' });
+page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Enveloppes' });
+page.getByRole('option', { name: /Accordé/i });
+
+// Text (for tags, error messages, toast notifications)
+page.getByText(/28 eure-et-loir/i);
+page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateRequired);
+```
+

+
+When a label appears in several sections (e.g. repeated blocs), use `.nth()`:
+
+```ts
+// nth(0) = first section, nth(1) = second section, etc.
+await expect
+  .element(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }).nth(0))
+  .toHaveDisplayValue('23-09-2024');
+await expect
+  .element(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }).nth(1))
+  .toHaveDisplayValue('08-04-2026');
+```
+

+
+```ts
+const envelopesGroup = page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Enveloppes' });
+const envelopeFields = envelopesGroup.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Enveloppe' });
+
+await expect.element(envelopeFields.nth(0)).toHaveDisplayValue('Légale ASSMAT');
+await expect.element(envelopeFields.nth(1)).toHaveDisplayValue('Légale SPE');
+```
+

+await expect.element(locator).toBeInTheDocument();
+await expect.element(locator).not.toBeInTheDocument();
+await expect.element(locator).toBeVisible();
+await expect.element(locator).toBeDisabled();
+await expect.element(locator).toBeChecked();
+await expect.element(locator).not.toBeChecked();

+await userEvent.keyboard('{Tab}');
+await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowDown}');

+```ts
+// Standard success mock
+worker.use(

+    HttpResponse.json(null, { status: 200 }),

+---
+
+## Date fields (InputDateV2)
+
+Dates are stored as `yyyy-MM-dd` internally and displayed as `dd-MM-yyyy`.
+
+| Stored value | Displayed value |
+| ------------ | --------------- |
+| `2024-09-23` | `23-09-2024`    |
+| `2026-04-08` | `08-04-2026`    |
+
+Assert displayed value:
+
+```ts
+await expect
+  .element(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }))
+  .toHaveDisplayValue('23-09-2024');
+```
+
+Clear a date and re-fill:
+
+```ts
+await page.getByRole('button', { name: "Vider le champ 'Date début'" }).click();
+await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }).fill('09-04-2026');
+```
+
+---
+
+## ComboBox / Select fields (InputSelectV2)
+
+The input's `aria-label` equals the `label` prop. The displayed value is the option label string.
+
+```ts
+// Assert selected value
+await expect.element(page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Statut' })).toHaveDisplayValue('Accordé'); // ALLOWED → 'Accordé'
+
+// Assert empty
+await expect.element(page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Statut' })).toHaveDisplayValue('');
+```
+
+---
+
+## Tag fields (InputMultiTagsSelectV2)
+
+Tags are rendered as visible text `${code} ${value}` (e.g. `28 Eure-et-Loir`).
+
+```ts
+// Single tag
+await expect.element(page.getByText(/28 eure-et-loir/i)).toBeInTheDocument();
+
+// Multiple tags with same text (e.g. territory + jurisprudence both = 33 Gironde)
+await expect.element(page.getByText(/33 gironde/i)).toHaveLength(2);
+```
+
+---
+
+## Checkbox groups (InputCheckboxV2)
+
+```ts

+  .not.toBeChecked();
+```
+
+Use `exact: true` when the label is a substring of another option (e.g. `'Flexi-présence'` vs `'Flexi-présence VAE'`).
+
+---
+
+## Validation testing pattern
+
+```ts
+testMsw('should validate form', async () => {
+  await renderComponent({});
+
+  // 1. Trigger validation by submitting empty form
+  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i }).click();
+
+  // 2. Assert all required-field errors appear
+  await expect.element(page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateRequired)).toBeVisible();
+
+  // 3. Fill fields and assert errors clear
+  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }).fill('01-04-2026');
+  await expect
+    .element(page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateRequired))
+    .not.toBeInTheDocument();
+
+  // 4. Test cross-field validation (e.g. start > end)
+  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date fin' }).fill('20-03-2026');
+  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i }).click();
+  await expect
+    .element(page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateMustBeBeforeEndDate))
+    .toBeVisible();
+});
+```
+
+---
+
+## Successful submission pattern
+
+```ts
+testMsw('should submit successfully', async ({ worker }) => {
+  worker.use(
+    http.put(endpoints.someEndpoint('id'), () => HttpResponse.json(null, { status: 200 })),
+  );
+  await renderComponent();
+
+  // fill fields...
+  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i }).click();
+
+  // Assert success toast (from react-hot-toast)
+  await expect.element(page.getByText(/success message/i)).toBeInTheDocument();
+});
+```
+
+---
+
+## Snapshot testing
+
+Snapshot tests are being phased out. Do NOT write new snapshot tests — use explicit assertions instead. Existing snapshots should be replaced with assertions when touching those test files.

-# Product Mission
-
-## Pitch
-
-IPERIA is a comprehensive training management platform that helps French home employment professionals (childcare providers, family assistants, and home care workers) access professional development and certifications by providing a unified system for discovering training programs, managing registrations, tracking certifications, and coordinating administrative workflows between learners, training agencies, and administrative staff.
-
-## Users
-
-### Primary Customers
-
-- **Home Employment Professionals**: Childcare providers, family assistants, and home care workers seeking professional training and certification to advance their careers and meet regulatory requirements.
-- **Training Agencies**: Organizations that deliver training programs and need to manage sessions, track attendance, issue certifications, and handle administrative processes.
-- **Administrative Staff**: IPERIA internal team members who oversee the training ecosystem, manage agencies, monitor quality, handle payments and refunds, and ensure compliance.
-
-### User Personas
-
-**Marie, Childcare Provider** (35-50 years old)
-
-- **Role:** Independent childcare provider caring for multiple children in her home
-- **Context:** Needs to maintain professional certifications and discover new training opportunities to improve her skills and meet employer requirements
-- **Pain Points:** Limited time between work commitments, difficulty finding relevant training near her location, confusion around eligibility and funding options
-- **Goals:** Quickly find and register for relevant training courses, track certification status, access training materials on her schedule
-
-**Sophie, Training Agency Coordinator** (30-45 years old)
-
-- **Role:** Administrative coordinator at a regional training agency
-- **Context:** Manages multiple training sessions simultaneously, coordinates with instructors and learners, handles documentation and reporting
-- **Pain Points:** Manual processes for attendance tracking, complex certification workflows, time-consuming administrative tasks, difficulty managing payments and refunds
-- **Goals:** Streamline session management, automate repetitive tasks, efficiently track learner progress, simplify billing and payment processes
-
-**Thomas, IPERIA Administrator** (28-40 years old)
-
-- **Role:** Internal operations manager overseeing training quality and compliance
-- **Context:** Monitors the entire training ecosystem across multiple agencies and regions
-- **Pain Points:** Lack of visibility into training quality metrics, difficult to audit compliance, time-consuming payment reconciliation, manual export processes
-- **Goals:** Real-time visibility into training operations, efficient quality monitoring, streamlined financial processes, data-driven decision making
-
-## The Problem
-
-### Fragmented Training Management
-
-The French home employment sector lacks a unified system for managing professional development. Training agencies, learners, and administrative staff rely on disconnected tools, manual processes, and paper-based workflows, resulting in inefficiencies, errors, and poor user experience. This fragmentation creates barriers to professional development for workers who already face time constraints and limited digital literacy.
-
-**Our Solution:** A centralized platform that integrates the entire training lifecycle from discovery through certification, with intuitive interfaces tailored to each user type and workflows optimized for the unique requirements of the home employment sector.
-
-### Complex Administrative Workflows
-
-Training management in this sector involves intricate processes: eligibility verification, funding coordination, multi-party approvals, document management, attendance tracking, certification issuance, and financial reconciliation. Manual handling of these processes leads to delays, errors, and compliance risks.
-
-**Our Solution:** Automated workflows with intelligent validation, role-based interfaces, status tracking, and integrated document management that guide users through complex processes while maintaining compliance and auditability.
-
-### Limited Accessibility for Non-Technical Users
-
-Home employment professionals often have limited time, varying levels of digital literacy, and access technology primarily through mobile devices. Generic platforms fail to meet their specific needs and context.
-
-**Our Solution:** A user-friendly interface designed for the target audience with simplified navigation, mobile-responsive design, and workflows optimized for the most common user tasks in the home employment training context.
-
-## Differentiators
-
-### Sector-Specific Design
-
-Unlike generic learning management systems, IPERIA is purpose-built for the French home employment sector. We provide specialized workflows for childcare and family assistant certifications, integration with sector-specific funding mechanisms, and interfaces designed around the unique needs of this professional community.
-
-This results in faster onboarding, higher user adoption, and workflows that match how the sector actually operates rather than forcing users to adapt to generic tools.
-
-### End-to-End Training Lifecycle Management
-
-Unlike point solutions that handle only course catalogs or only certification, IPERIA manages the complete journey from training discovery through certification issuance and beyond. We integrate learner management, session coordination, attendance tracking, assessment, certification, payments, and reporting in a single platform.
-
-This results in reduced duplicate data entry, seamless handoffs between process stages, better visibility for all stakeholders, and a single source of truth for training data.
-
-### Multi-Stakeholder Coordination
-
-Unlike learner-only or agency-only platforms, IPERIA serves the entire ecosystem. We provide tailored experiences for learners, training agencies, and administrative staff while enabling seamless coordination between them through shared workflows and real-time status updates.
-
-This results in faster approvals, fewer communication gaps, improved transparency, and more efficient resolution of issues that require cross-stakeholder coordination.
-
-## Key Features
-
-### Core Features
-
-- **Training Catalog & Discovery:** Browse available training programs with filtering by location, category, schedule, and eligibility. View detailed program information including learning objectives, prerequisites, duration, and certification outcomes.
-
-- **Registration & Enrollment:** Complete training registrations with guided workflows that verify eligibility, collect required documents, and route approvals to appropriate stakeholders. Track registration status in real-time.
-
-- **Session Management:** Create and manage training sessions with scheduling, capacity management, location coordination, and instructor assignment. Handle cancellations, rescheduling, and participant communications.
-
-- **Attendance Tracking:** Record and verify learner attendance across training sessions with support for various attendance models (in-person, remote, hybrid). Generate attendance reports and certificates.
-

-
-### Administrative Features
-
-- **User & Agency Management:** Manage users across different roles (learners, instructors, agency staff, administrators) and training agencies with configurable permissions, agency relationships, and user lifecycles.

-
-- **Document Management:** Upload, store, organize, and share training-related documents with version control, access controls, and document lifecycle management. Generate documents from templates.
-
-- **Workflow & Approval Management:** Configurable multi-stage approval workflows with status tracking, notification routing, and escalation handling. Support for complex business rules and validation.
-
-### Advanced Features
-
-- **Reporting & Analytics:** Generate comprehensive reports on training activity, learner progress, agency performance, and financial metrics. Export data in various formats for external analysis.
-
-- **Feature Flags & Configuration:** Enable controlled rollout of new features and behavior customization through feature flags. Configure system behavior without code deployment.
-
-- **Export Management:** Automated export of data to external systems (financial, regulatory, partner systems) with scheduled exports, format transformation, and error handling.
-
-- **Geolocation & Maps:** Interactive maps for finding training locations, viewing agency coverage areas, and optimizing training accessibility based on learner locations.

-## Current State Assessment

-# React Guidelines
-
-## Core Guidelines
-
-- Enable React Strict Mode
-- Embrace latest React features (Suspense, `use()`, `useTransition()`, etc.)
-- NEVER use `import * as React from 'react'` - import specifically what you need
-
-## Component Structure
-
-- Use functional components with `function` keyword
-- Strongly type `props` with `PropsWithChildren` type when receiving children
-- Use spread/rest operators for props and state management
-- Extract reusable logic into custom hooks
-
-## Hooks
-
-- Follow the Rules of Hooks (only call at top level, not in loops/conditions)
-- Use appropriate dependency arrays in useEffect
-- Always use a proper named function for useEffect callbacks
-- Implement cleanup in useEffect when needed (timers, listeners, subscriptions)
-- Implement useReducer for complex state logic
-
-## Component Organization
-
-- Apply SOLID principles to React
-- Split into sub-components by responsibility
-- Move shared components outside the parent folder
-- Create private sub-components for single use
-- Prefer local state + hook-based data fetching — the smart/dumb container pattern is legacy and must NOT be used for new components
-
-## State Management and Data
-
-- Use **TanStack Query** for server state (data fetching, caching, mutations)
-- Use **Redux** for existing global state only — do NOT create new Redux state or reducers
-- Use local `useState` / `useReducer` for component-level state
-- Declare calculated variables at the top of components
-- Implement proper state lifting patterns
-- Avoid prop drilling through proper state management
-
-## Suspense
-
-- Use Suspense for loading states and code splitting
-- Wrap async components with Suspense boundaries
-- Provide meaningful fallback UI during loading
-- Combine Suspense with Error Boundaries for error handling
-
-## Performance Optimization
-
-- Leverage React Compiler for automatic optimization
-- Trust compiler's automatic memoization (NEVER use manual `useMemo` or `useCallback`)
-- Use React.memo for expensive components when React Compiler isn't available
-- Implement proper key props for lists
-- Use React DevTools Profiler to identify bottlenecks
-
-## Forms
-
-- Use **React Hook Form + Zod** for all new forms
-- Redux-Form is legacy — do not use for new forms
-- Use **controlled components** for form inputs — wire them via RHF's `Controller` (or `useController`)
-- Use the existing **v2 input components** (e.g. `InputTextV2`, `InputSelectV2`, etc.) which are already built for RHF integration — do not roll custom inputs or use legacy uncontrolled inputs
-- Handle form submission states properly (loading, success, error)
-
-## Error Handling
-
-- Implement Error Boundaries for catching component errors
-- Handle async errors properly with try-catch or error states
-- Implement proper fallback UI for error states
-
-## Testing
-
-- Use **Vitest browser mode** (`*.browser.test.tsx`) for component and integration tests
-- Use plain Vitest (`*.test.ts`) for pure functions and utilities only
-- Test user interactions and behaviour, not implementation details
-- Refer to `agent-os/standards/testing/test-writing.md` for detailed patterns
-
-## Accessibility
-
-- Use semantic HTML elements
-- Implement proper ARIA attributes when needed
-- Handle focus management in dynamic content

-# Test Writing Standards
-
-## Core principles
-
-- **Test behavior, not implementation**: focus on what the code does, not how
-- **Test only core user flows**: critical paths and primary workflows first; skip non-critical utilities
-- **Defer edge cases**: unless business-critical, address in dedicated testing phases
-- **Write minimal tests during development**: complete the feature first, then add tests at logical completion points
-- **Clear test names**: describe what is tested and the expected outcome
-- **Fast execution**: keep unit tests in milliseconds so they run frequently
-
----
-
-## Unit tests (non-browser)
-
-Unit tests run in Node — no browser, no DOM. Use them exclusively for pure functions and utilities.
-
-### Imports
-
-```ts
-import { describe, it, test, expect, vi, beforeAll, afterAll, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
-```
-
-### Pure functions
-
-```ts
-describe('pluralize()', () => {
-  it('returns singular when count is 1', () => {
-    expect(pluralize(1, 'évaluation')).toBe('1 évaluation');
-  });
-
-  it('returns plural when count > 1', () => {
-    expect(pluralize(2, 'évaluation')).toBe('2 évaluations');
-  });
-});
-```
-
-### Mocking
-
-```ts
-// Function mock
-const onClose = vi.fn();
-
-// Spy on a module export
-const spy = vi.spyOn(myModule, 'someFunction');
-expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedArg);
-
-// Mock global / Date
-beforeAll(() => {
-  Date.now = vi.fn(() => new Date('2024-01-01').valueOf());
-});
-afterAll(() => {
-  global.Date.now = realNow;
-});
-
-// Reset between tests
-beforeEach(() => {
-  vi.clearAllMocks();
-});
-```
-
-### Assertions
-
-```ts
-expect(result).toBe(10);
-expect(result).toEqual({ key: 'value' });
-expect(result).toBeCloseTo(7.65);
-expect(result).toBeTruthy();
-expect(result).toBeNull();
-
-expect(mockFn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedArg);
-expect(mockFn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
-```
-
----
-
-## Component / Integration tests (browser)
-
-These tests run in a real browser (Chromium via Playwright). Use them for anything involving React components, user interactions, form behaviour, or API calls.
-
-- **File naming**: `*.browser.test.tsx`
-- **Render helper**: `renderWithProviders` from `@/test/browser-test-utils/renderWithProviders`
-- **Test runner**: `test` for no API, `testMsw` for API mocking (MSW worker auto-managed)
-- **Queries**: `page` locator from `vitest/browser` — prefer `getByRole`
-- **Assertions**: `await expect.element(locator).*`
-- **Interactions**: `locator.click()`, `locator.fill()`, `userEvent.keyboard()`
-
----
-
-## File conventions
-
-- Browser integration tests: `*.browser.test.tsx`
-- Unit / helper tests: `*.test.ts` (no browser needed)
-- Location: `src/**/__tests__/ComponentName.browser.test.tsx`
-
----
-
-## Imports
-
-```ts
-import { describe, expect, vi, test } from 'vitest';
-import { page, userEvent } from 'vitest/browser';
-import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
-
-import { renderWithProviders } from '@/test/browser-test-utils/renderWithProviders';
-import { testMsw } from '@/test/browser-test-utils/test-extend';
-```
-
----
-
-## `test` vs `testMsw`
-
-|           | `test`           | `testMsw`                           |
-| --------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- |
-| Use when  | No API calls     | Component makes API calls           |
-| Worker    | None             | Auto-started, reset after each test |
-| Signature | `async () => {}` | `async ({ worker }) => {}`          |
-
-```ts
-// No API — use test
-test('should render correctly', async () => {
-  await renderComponent();
-});
-
-// Has API — use testMsw
-testMsw('should submit form', async ({ worker }) => {
-  worker.use(
-    http.put(endpoints.someEndpoint('id'), () => HttpResponse.json(null, { status: 200 })),
-  );
-  await renderComponent();
-});
-```
-
-Optionally set timeout when the test loads async data:
-
-```ts
-testMsw('should load data', { timeout: 30000 }, async ({ worker }) => { ... });
-```
-
----
-
-## `renderWithProviders`
-
-```ts
-await renderWithProviders(<MyComponent />, {
-  preloadedState?: Partial<RootState>,   // Redux initial state
-  pathname?: string,                     // Current route (default: '/')
-  initialEntries?: string[],             // Router history entries
-  withQueryClient?: boolean,             // true when component uses TanStack Query
-  withRouter?: boolean,                  // false to disable router wrapper
-  useReducerGenerator?: boolean,         // true for legacy reducer-generated reducers
-});
-```
-
-Typical pattern — define once, reuse across tests:
-
-```ts
-function renderComponent(props = defaultProps) {
-  return renderWithProviders(
-    <MyForm {...props} />,
-    { withQueryClient: true, withRouter: false },
-  );
-}
-```
-
----
-
-## Querying elements
-
-Prefer `getByRole` with accessible name. Fall back to `getByText` only for non-interactive content.

-```ts
-// Roles
-page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i });
-page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }); // matches "Date début*" too (substring)
-page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Statut' });
-page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Présentiel' });
-page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Présentiel' });
-page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Enveloppes' });
-page.getByRole('option', { name: /Accordé/i });
-
-// Text (for tags, error messages, toast notifications)
-page.getByText(/28 eure-et-loir/i);
-page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateRequired);
-```
-
-### Multiple matches — use `.nth()`
-
-When a label appears in several sections (e.g. repeated blocs), use `.nth()`:
-
-```ts
-// nth(0) = first section, nth(1) = second section, etc.
-await expect
-  .element(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }).nth(0))
-  .toHaveDisplayValue('23-09-2024');
-await expect
-  .element(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date début' }).nth(1))
-  .toHaveDisplayValue('08-04-2026');
-```
-

-
-```ts
-const envelopesGroup = page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Enveloppes' });

-```ts
-await expect.element(locator).toBeInTheDocument();
-await expect.element(locator).not.toBeInTheDocument();

-await expect.element(locator).toBeDisabled();

-```ts

-
-```ts

-    HttpResponse.json(null, { status: 200 }),

-  .not.toBeChecked();

-## Validation testing pattern
-
-```ts
-testMsw('should validate form', async () => {
-  await renderComponent({});
-

-    .element(page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateRequired))
-    .not.toBeInTheDocument();

-  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Date fin' }).fill('20-03-2026');
-  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i }).click();
-  await expect
-    .element(page.getByText(FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.date.startDateMustBeBeforeEndDate))

-});
-```
-

-
-## Successful submission pattern
-
-```ts
-testMsw('should submit successfully', async ({ worker }) => {
-  worker.use(
-    http.put(endpoints.someEndpoint('id'), () => HttpResponse.json(null, { status: 200 })),

-
-  // fill fields...
-  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /valider/i }).click();

-  // Assert success toast (from react-hot-toast)

-# Spec: RIB Data Display with GDPR Compliance
-
-## ADDED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Default masking of RIB data
-
-The system SHALL mask all IBAN and BIC data by default on initial display, regardless of user permissions.
-
-#### Scenario: Initial page load with RIB data
-
-- **WHEN** a user loads any page displaying RIB information
-- **THEN** IBAN display depends on user permissions (see RG2, RG4, RG5)
-- **AND** BIC display depends on user permissions (see RG2, RG4, RG5)
-- **AND** Titulaire (account holder) is displayed in clear text
-- **AND** masking applies by default to all users, including those with full permissions
-- **NOTE** Masked characters use "\*\*\*" (not "XXX") as some BIC codes contain the letter X
-
-#### Scenario: Page reload resets masking state
-
-- **WHEN** a user has revealed RIB data using the toggle button
-- **AND** the user reloads the page
-- **THEN** IBAN and BIC return to their masked state
-- **AND** the toggle button returns to "Afficher le RIB" state
-
-#### Scenario: Navigation resets masking state
-
-- **WHEN** a user has revealed RIB data using the toggle button
-- **AND** the user navigates to another page
-- **AND** the user returns to the page with RIB data
-- **THEN** IBAN and BIC are displayed in their masked state
-- **AND** the toggle button returns to "Afficher le RIB" state
-
-### Requirement: Permission-based toggle button visibility
-
-The system SHALL display or hide the RIB toggle button based on user permissions.
-
-**Actual permissions implemented**: `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_FULL`, `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_PARTIAL`, `REGISTRATION_RIB_WRITE`
-
-#### Scenario: User with full read access sees toggle button
-
-- **WHEN** a user has the `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_FULL` permission
-- **AND** the user views a page with RIB data
-- **THEN** a button labeled "Afficher le RIB" is visible
-- **AND** the button is enabled and clickable (unless fields are dirty)
-
-#### Scenario: User with write access sees toggle button
-
-- **WHEN** a user has the `REGISTRATION_RIB_WRITE` permission
-- **AND** the user views a page with RIB data
-- **THEN** a button labeled "Afficher le RIB" is visible
-- **AND** the button is enabled and clickable (unless fields are dirty)
-
-#### Scenario: User with partial access sees partial data
-
-- **WHEN** a user has only the `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_PARTIAL` permission
-- **AND** the user views a page with RIB data
-- **THEN** IBAN displays last 3 characters: "\***\* \*\*** \***\* \*\*** \*\*\*\* " + last 3 chars
-- **AND** BIC displays last 3 characters: "**\***" + last 3 chars
-- **AND** toggle button is not displayed (no full access)
-
-#### Scenario: User with no permissions sees no toggle button
-
-- **WHEN** a user has none of the RIB data access permissions
-- **AND** the user views a page with RIB data
-- **THEN** no toggle button is displayed
-- **AND** IBAN is fully masked as "\***\* \*\*** \***\* \*\*** \***\* \*\***"
-- **AND** BIC is fully masked as "**\*\*\*\***"
-
-#### Scenario: No RIB data entered
-
-- **WHEN** RIB data is empty or contains only "-" characters
-- **THEN** no toggle button is displayed
-- **AND** the user can enter new RIB data if they have write permissions
-
-### Requirement: Toggle button functionality
-
-The system SHALL reveal or mask RIB data when the toggle button is clicked, according to user permissions.
-
-#### Scenario: User with full access reveals RIB data
-
-- **WHEN** a user with `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_FULL` or `REGISTRATION_RIB_WRITE` permission clicks "Afficher le RIB"
-- **THEN** `useRibFormat` hook updates `ribIsUnmasked` state to `true`
-- **AND** `selectRibFormat` returns 'FULL' format
-- **AND** React Hook Form's `resetField` updates form values with full IBAN, BIC, and owner
-- **AND** IBAN displays in full clear text
-- **AND** BIC displays in full clear text
-- **AND** Titulaire displays in full (was always visible)
-- **AND** the button label changes to "Masquer le RIB"
-- **AND** the revealed data remains visible until masked again, page reload, or navigation
-
-#### Scenario: User masks revealed RIB data
-
-- **WHEN** a user has revealed RIB data
-- **AND** the user clicks "Masquer le RIB"
-- **THEN** `useRibFormat` hook updates `ribIsUnmasked` state to `false`
-- **AND** `selectRibFormat` returns 'PARTIAL_MASKED' format
-- **AND** React Hook Form's `resetField` updates form values with partial masked data
-- **AND** IBAN returns to partial masked state "\***\* \*\*** \***\* \*\*** \*\*\*\* " + last 3 chars
-- **AND** BIC returns to partial masked state "**\***" + last 3 chars
-- **AND** the button label changes back to "Afficher le RIB"
-
-#### Scenario: User with partial access cannot toggle
-
-- **WHEN** a user with only `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_PARTIAL` permission views RIB data
-- **THEN** `canReadRibDataFull` permission check returns false
-- **AND** toggle button is not displayed (Activity mode='hidden')
-- **AND** IBAN shows last 3 characters only (PARTIAL_MASKED format)
-- **AND** BIC shows last 3 characters only (PARTIAL_MASKED format)
-
-### Requirement: Permission-based field editability
-
-The system SHALL enable or disable RIB field editing based on user permissions.
-
-#### Scenario: User with write permission can edit fields
-
-- **WHEN** a user has the `REGISTRATION_RIB_WRITE` permission
-- **AND** the user is in edit mode (e.g., EditTrainingDeparture form)
-- **AND** RIB data is not anonymized (`ribIsAnonymized` is false or undefined)
-- **THEN** `canEditRibField` evaluates to true
-- **AND** Titulaire field is editable (`disabled={!canEditRibField}`)
-- **AND** IBAN field is editable with IBAN_MASK applied
-- **AND** BIC field is editable with BIC_MASK applied
-- **AND** a "RÉINITIALISER" button is visible and enabled
-
-#### Scenario: User with read-only permission cannot edit fields
-
-- **WHEN** a user has only the `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_FULL` permission
-- **AND** the user is viewing RIB data
-- **THEN** `canEditRibField` evaluates to false
-- **AND** all RIB fields (Titulaire, IBAN, BIC) are disabled (read-only)
-- **AND** the "RÉINITIALISER" button is disabled
-
-#### Scenario: User with no write permission in edit mode
-
-- **WHEN** a user without `REGISTRATION_RIB_WRITE` permission is in edit mode
-- **THEN** `hasWriteRibPermission` evaluates to false
-- **AND** `canEditRibField` evaluates to false
-- **AND** RIB fields are disabled (read-only)
-- **AND** the "RÉINITIALISER" button is disabled
-- **AND** the user cannot modify RIB data even if other form fields are editable
-

-

-- **AND** fields display anonymized data without formatting
-- **AND** editing is prevented regardless of write permission

-# Proposal: Add GDPR-Compliant RIB Data Masking
-
-## Why
-
-To comply with GDPR regulations, IPERIA must limit access to sensitive banking information (RIB data: IBAN, BIC) in the application. Currently, RIB data is displayed in plain text to all users, creating privacy and security risks, especially during screen sharing sessions. This poses a regulatory compliance issue and increases the risk of data exposure.
-
-## What Changes
-
-### Permission System
-
-- Implement 3 new permissions for RIB data access control:
-  - `rib_data_partial_access:read` - View last 3 characters only of IBAN/BIC
-  - `rib_data_total_access:read` - View full IBAN/BIC (read-only)
-  - `rib_data_total_access:write` - View and modify full IBAN/BIC
-
-### Display Behavior
-
-1. **Default state**: All RIB data (IBAN, BIC) masked by default for all users
-2. **Toggle button**: "Afficher/Masquer le RIB" button to reveal/hide data based on permissions
-3. **Account holder**: Always visible regardless of permissions
-4. **Permission-based masking**:
-   - No permission: IBAN/BIC fully masked (XXXX...), no toggle button
-   - Partial permission: Last 3 characters visible, disabled toggle button with warning
-   - Read permission: Full reveal with toggle button, read-only fields
-   - Write permission: Full reveal with toggle button, editable fields + "RÉINITIALISER" button
-
-### Affected Locations
-
-RIB data masking implemented in the following forms:
-
-1. **Cadre de départ en formation** (Training Departure) - Edit mode (`EditTrainingDeparture`)
-2. **Cadre de départ en évaluation** (Evaluation Departure) - Edit mode (`EditEvaluationDeparture`)
-3. **Paiements** (Payments) - Edit mode (`PaymentForm`)
-4. **Opération corrective** (Corrective Operation) - Edit mode (`CorrectiveOperationForm`)
-
-**Note**: Additional contexts (read-only banking details views, frozen data exports, RIB document access control) were planned but not included in this implementation phase.
-
-### Specs Updated
-
-- `rib-data-display`: New capability for permission-based RIB data masking and display
-
-## Context
-
-IPERIA manages sensitive banking information for training participants and organizations. GDPR regulations require strict access controls on personal financial data. The current implementation displays RIB data in plain text, which:
-
-- Violates GDPR data minimization principles
-- Creates security risks during screen sharing
-- Provides unnecessary access to sensitive financial data
-- Lacks audit trail for data access
-
-## Problem Statement
-
-According to JIRA issue IPERIA-8101:
-
-1. RIB data is currently visible to all users without restrictions
-2. No mechanism exists to control access based on user roles/permissions
-3. No way to temporarily hide data during screen sharing
-4. Document access in validation SAS is not restricted
-
-## Proposed Solution
-
-Implement a permission-based masking system that:
-
-1. **Masks by default**: All IBAN/BIC masked on page load (even for authorized users)
-2. **Permission gates**: Backend provides user permissions, frontend enforces display rules
-3. **Toggle control**: Button to show/hide (like password fields) for authorized users
-4. **Progressive disclosure**: Show only what user is permitted to see
-5. **State management**: Masking resets on page reload/navigation
-
-## Affected Components
-
-### Frontend Components
-
-- `RibForm` (src/components/presentational/common/RibForm/RibForm.tsx) - Main RIB form component refactored for masking
-- `RibToggleButton` (src/components/presentational/common/RibForm/components/RibToggleButton.tsx) - Toggle button for show/hide functionality
-- `useRibFormat` (src/hooks/useRibFormat.ts) - Hook managing RIB data formatting and masking
-- `useTrainingDepartureRibFormat` (src/hooks/data/rib/useTrainingDepartureRibFormat.ts) - Training-specific RIB formatting
-- `useGetRib` (src/hooks/data/rib/useGetRib.ts) - React Query hook for fetching RIB data
-- `selectRibFormat` (src/components/presentational/common/RibForm/helpers.ts) - Format selector utility
-- `formatRibValues` (src/components/presentational/common/RibForm/formatRibValues.ts) - RIB values formatter
-- `useRibFieldDirtyTracking` (src/components/presentational/common/RibForm/useRibFieldDirtyTracking.ts) - Dirty field tracking
-- `usePermission` hook integration for permission checks
-
-### Form Components Updated
-
-1. **EditTrainingDeparture** - Training departure form with masked RIB
-2. **EditEvaluationDeparture** - Evaluation departure form with masked RIB
-3. **PaymentForm** - Payment form with masked RIB
-4. **CorrectiveOperationForm** - Corrective operation form with masked RIB
-
-### Backend Integration
-
-- New API endpoint: `GET /training-departures/{id}/rib`
-- `RibDTO` model with `formats` array containing 3 format variants (FULL_MASKED, PARTIAL_MASKED, FULL)
-- `AuthenticatedUserDTO` updated with new permission types
-
-### Permissions Added
-
-- `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_FULL` - View full IBAN/BIC (read-only)
-- `REGISTRATION_RIB_READ_PARTIAL` - View last 3 characters only
-- `REGISTRATION_RIB_WRITE` - View and modify full IBAN/BIC
-
-## Impact Analysis
-
-### User Experience
-
-- **Positive**: Enhanced privacy and GDPR compliance
-- **Positive**: Reduces accidental exposure during screen sharing
-- **Positive**: Clear visual feedback on permission levels
-- **Neutral**: Users with full permissions have same access (just one click to reveal)
-- **Neutral**: Users without permissions already shouldn't access RIB data
-
-### Security Considerations
-
-- **High**: Permission enforcement must happen server-side (frontend is display only)
-- **Medium**: Masking state must not persist across sessions
-- **Low**: Toggle state managed in component state (resets on unmount/reload)
-
-### Technical Considerations
-
-- Reusable toggle button component for consistency
-- Permission checks using existing `hasPermission` helper
-- Masking logic extracted to utility functions
-- State management via React hooks (no Redux needed)
-- Backend provides permissions and full data; frontend masks display
-
-### Risks
-
-- **Low**: Feature is primarily display logic, minimal breaking changes
-- **Medium**: Must ensure backend validates permissions on all RIB-related endpoints
-- **Low**: Performance impact negligible (client-side masking)
-
-## Success Criteria
-
-✅ **Implemented:**
-
-1. By default, all IBAN/BIC data is masked on initial page load
-2. Users see toggle button only if they have read/write permissions
-3. Clicking toggle reveals data according to permission level:
-   - Partial: Last 3 characters visible (PARTIAL_MASKED format)
-   - Full: Complete IBAN/BIC visible (FULL format)
-4. Account holder (Titulaire) always visible
-5. Users with write permission can edit fields when data is not anonymized
-6. "RÉINITIALISER" button visible and enabled only for write permission users
-7. Masking resets on page reload or navigation (state managed in React component)
-8. Backend provides three format variants, frontend selects based on permissions
-9. Toggle button disabled when RIB fields are dirty (prevents data loss)
-10. Implemented in 4 key forms: EditTrainingDeparture, EditEvaluationDeparture, PaymentForm, CorrectiveOperationForm
-
-⏳ **Deferred to future phases:**
-
-- Read-only banking details views (PE/Cadre details)
-- Export remboursements frozen data with icon-only toggle
-- RIB document access control in validation SAS
-
-## Implementation Notes
-
-### Architecture Decisions
-
-1. **Backend-driven masking**: Backend provides 3 pre-formatted variants (FULL_MASKED, PARTIAL_MASKED, FULL) rather than frontend masking logic. This ensures consistent formatting and reduces security risks.
-
-2. **Hook-based state management**: Created `useRibFormat` hook to manage masking state and format selection. This centralizes logic and makes it reusable across forms.
-
-3. **Form-specific hooks**: `useTrainingDepartureRibFormat` wraps `useRibFormat` and `useGetRib` to provide a complete solution for training departure forms.
-
-4. **React Hook Form integration**: Toggle functionality integrated with React Hook Form's `resetField` to update form values when revealing/masking data.
-
-5. **Dirty field protection**: Toggle button disables when RIB fields are modified to prevent accidental data loss.
-
-6. **Permission-based rendering**: Used `usePermission` hook with new permission types to control UI elements visibility and enablement.
-
-7. **Activity component for toggle**: Used React 19's `Activity` component to control toggle button visibility rather than conditional rendering.
-
-### Key Technical Patterns
-
-- **Format selection strategy**: `selectRibFormat` utility implements logic to choose correct format based on permissions and toggle state
-- **RIB value formatting**: `formatRibValues` handles edge cases like empty RIB data and reset operations
-- **MSW mocking**: Added comprehensive MSW handlers for RIB endpoints to support development and testing
-
-## References
-
-- JIRA Issue: IPERIA-8160 (originally IPERIA-8101)
-- Branch: `feat/IPERIA-8160`
-- Commits: 5 commits implementing the feature across different forms
-- Backend API endpoint: `/training-departures/{id}/rib`
-- RGPD/GDPR compliance requirements

-## Overview
-
-This design document outlines the technical implementation for adding permission-based reuse of Parcours Modules (PM) and Actions d'Évaluation (AE) across different Parcours Blocs (PB).
-
-## Architecture Decisions
-
-### 1. Permission Checking Strategy
-
-**Decision**: Use the existing `hasPermission` helper function from `src/helpers/roles.ts`
-
-**Rationale**:
-
-- Consistent with existing permission patterns in the codebase
-- Already integrated with Redux state management
-- Well-tested and reliable
-
-**Implementation**:
-
-```typescript
-const canReuseLinkedItems = hasPermission(
-  { permissions: userPermissions },
-  PermissionTypes.BLOC_PATH_BYPASS_UNIQUE_COMMON_TRAINING_CONSTRAINT,
-);
-```
-
-### 2. Data Flow Architecture
-
-**Decision**: Enhance existing Redux data flow without breaking changes
-
-**Components**:
-
-1. **API Layer**: Backend provides linked PB information in PM/AE responses
-2. **Redux Actions**: Existing actions handle the enhanced data
-3. **Redux State**: Store linked PB information in existing state structure
-4. **Components**: Conditionally render based on permission and linked status
-
-**Data Structure Enhancement**:
-
-**Note**: After backend implementation, we discovered that the `blocPaths` array already exists in `SearchModulePathDTO` and `SearchEvaluationDTO`. Instead of adding a new `linkedBlocPath` field, we use the existing structure:
-
-```typescript
-interface SearchModulePathDTO {
-  // ... existing fields
-  blocPaths: LightBlocPathDTO[]; // Already exists, contains all linked PBs
-}
-
-interface SearchEvaluationDTO {
-  // ... existing fields
-  blocPaths: LightBlocPathDTO[]; // Already exists, contains all linked PBs
-}
-
-interface LightBlocPathDTO {
-  id: string;
-  code: string;
-  name?: string;
-}
-```
-
-### 3. UI Component Strategy
-
-**Decision**: Extend existing components rather than creating new ones
-
-**Rationale**:
-
-- Minimizes code duplication
-- Maintains consistency with existing UI patterns
-- Easier to maintain backward compatibility
-
-**Implementation Pattern**:
-
-**Actual Implementation**: Filtering is done at the API/backend level, not in the component:
-
-```typescript
-// In ModulePathsList component
-interface ModulePathsListProps {
-  // ... existing props
-  hasReusePermission: boolean;
-}
-
-// Helper function to determine query parameter
-// src/components/presentational/BlocPathForm/getLinkedToBlocPathFromPermission.ts
-export function getLinkedToBlocPathFromPermission(
-  hasReusePermission: boolean,
-): boolean | undefined {
-  return hasReusePermission ? undefined : false;
-}
-
-// API call with linkedToBlocPath parameter
-// - undefined: backend returns ALL module paths (with and without links)
-// - false: backend returns ONLY unlinked module paths
-modulePathActions.listForBlocPathFromModuleCode(item, trainingAgencyCode, {
-  linkedToBlocPath: getLinkedToBlocPathFromPermission(hasReusePermission),
-});

-### 5. Modal Implementation

-# Proposal: Add Permission for Reusing PM/AE Across Parcours Blocs
-
-## Why
-
-Training Organizations (OFs) are creating duplicate Parcours Modules (PM) and Actions d'Évaluation (AE) because they cannot reuse existing ones that are already linked to other Parcours Blocs (PBs). This duplication wastes time, creates data redundancy, and complicates maintenance. By allowing authorized users to reuse linked PM/AE across multiple PBs, we can significantly improve efficiency and reduce administrative overhead.
-
-## What Changes
-
-### Frontend Changes
-
-1. **Permission-based filtering**: Add `BLOC_PATH_BYPASS_UNIQUE_COMMON_TRAINING_CONSTRAINT` permission check to control PM/AE visibility
-2. **API integration**: Update PM/AE search to pass `linkedToBlocPath` parameter based on permission
-3. **Visual indicators**: Display linked PB information in PM/AE lists for users with permission
-4. **Confirmation modal**: Show confirmation dialog when selecting already-linked PM/AE
-5. **Component updates**:
-   - `ModulePathsList`: Add linked PB display and permission-based filtering
-   - `EvaluationsList`: Add linked PB display and permission-based filtering
-   - `BlocPathForm`: Integrate confirmation modal for linked selections
-
-### Specs Updated
-
-- `pb-module-path-selection`: Permission-based module path visibility requirements
-- `pb-evaluation-selection`: Permission-based evaluation selection requirements
-
-## Context
-
-Currently, when creating or editing a Parcours Bloc (PB), Training Organizations (OF) can only see and select Parcours Modules (PM) and Actions d'Évaluation (AE) that are not already linked to other PBs. This limitation prevents OFs from efficiently reusing existing PM/AE configurations across multiple PBs, leading to unnecessary duplication of effort.
-
-## Problem Statement
-
-According to JIRA issue IPERIA-8164, OFs need the ability to:
-
-1. Reuse existing PM and AE that are already linked to other PBs
-2. Have visibility of which PB a PM/AE is already linked to
-3. Receive confirmation when selecting an already-linked PM/AE
-
-This functionality needs to be controlled by a permission created by the backend (IPERIA-8165).
-
-## Proposed Solution
-
-Implement a permission-based system that:
-
-1. **Without permission**: Shows only unlinked PM/AE (current behavior)
-2. **With permission**:
-   - Shows ALL PM/AE created by the selected OF
-   - Visually separates linked from unlinked items
-   - Displays which PB each linked item belongs to
-   - Shows a confirmation modal when selecting linked items
-
-## Affected Components
-
-### Frontend Components
-
-- `BlocPathForm` - Main form for creating/editing PB
-- `ModulePathsList` - Component displaying available PM
-- `EvaluationsList` - Component displaying available AE
-- Permission checking utilities in `src/helpers/roles.ts`
-
-### User Flows
-
-1. **Creation flow** (`/ajout-parcours-bloc`)
-2. **Edit flow** (`/modification-parcours-bloc/:blocPathId`)
-
-## Impact Analysis
-
-### User Experience
-
-- **Positive**: OFs with permission can efficiently reuse existing configurations
-- **Positive**: Clear visual distinction between linked/unlinked items prevents confusion
-- **Positive**: Confirmation modal prevents accidental linking
-- **Neutral**: Users without permission see no change
-
-### Technical Considerations
-
-- Permission check will be performed using the existing `hasPermission` helper
-- Backend will provide the permission flag and linked PB information in API responses
-- Modal component will be reused from existing design system
-
-### Risks
-
-- **Low**: Feature is additive and backward-compatible
-- **Low**: Permission-gated, so rollout can be controlled
-
-## Success Criteria
-
-1. Users with permission can see ALL PM/AE from their OF
-2. Linked items are visually distinguished with PB reference
-3. Confirmation modal appears when selecting linked items
-4. Users without permission maintain current behavior
-5. All selections are properly validated and saved
-
-## Timeline
-
-Estimated implementation: 3-4 days
-
-- Day 1: Update API integration and data models
-- Day 2: Implement UI changes for PM selection
-- Day 3: Implement UI changes for AE selection
-- Day 4: Add confirmation modal and testing
-
-## References
-
-- JIRA Issue: IPERIA-8164 (Frontend implementation)
-- JIRA Issue: IPERIA-8165 (Backend permission creation)
-- Mockups: Provided in JIRA ticket

-## MODIFIED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Test Helper Functions
-
-The testing utilities SHALL provide modern, composable helpers for rendering components. Use the minimal wrapper needed.
-
-#### Scenario: Component needs no providers
-
-- **WHEN** a component does not use Redux, Router, or other providers
-- **THEN** use direct `render(<Component {...props} />)` from `@testing-library/react`
-- **AND** no wrapper is needed
-
-#### Scenario: Component needs Redux store
-
-- **WHEN** a component needs Redux store and/or Router
-- **THEN** use `renderWithProviders(<Component {...props} />)`
-- **AND** the component receives a fresh test store instance
-
-#### Scenario: Render component with children
-
-- **WHEN** a test needs to render a component with children
-- **THEN** use `renderWithProviders(<Component {...props}>{children}</Component>)`
-
-#### Scenario: Component uses Redux-Form internally
-
-- **WHEN** a component uses Redux-Form deep in its abstraction
-- **THEN** use `renderWithProviders(<Component {...props} />, { useReduxForm: true })`
-
-#### Scenario: Component uses useListRouting or API middleware
-
-- **WHEN** a component uses `useListRouting` hook or dispatches API actions
-- **THEN** use `renderWithProviders(<Component {...props} />, { useReduxApiMiddleware: true })`
-
-#### Scenario: Component needs initial route entries
-
-- **WHEN** a component depends on router state
-- **THEN** use `renderWithProviders(<Component {...props} />, { initialEntries: ['/path'] })`
-
-#### Scenario: Component uses Redux-Form (form component tests)
-
-- **WHEN** a test needs to render a Redux-Form connected component
-- **THEN** use `renderWithReduxFormAndProviders(Component, { formName, props })`
-- **AND** optionally pass `validator` and `valueSelector` if needed

-# Mandate Operation Billing Specification
-
-## MODIFIED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Billing Generation Confirmation
-
-The system SHALL allow administrators to generate mandate operation billing through a confirmation modal using TanStack Query for API calls and Activity component for conditional rendering.
-
-#### Scenario: User confirms billing generation
-
-- **WHEN** user clicks "Generate Bill" button in the billing list
-- **AND** modal opens with confirmation message
-- **AND** user clicks "Oui" (Yes) button
-- **THEN** system sends POST request to `/api/mandate-operations/{training_departure_id}/billing-requested`
-- **AND** system displays "Traitement en cours..." message with loader
-- **AND** system hides action buttons during request
-- **AND** system shows success message on success response
-- **AND** system shows "Fermer" button after completion
-
-#### Scenario: User cancels billing generation
-
-- **WHEN** user clicks "Generate Bill" button
-- **AND** modal opens with confirmation message
-- **AND** user clicks "Non" (No) button
-- **THEN** system closes modal without making API call
-- **AND** system returns to billing list view
-
-#### Scenario: API request fails
-
-- **WHEN** billing generation API request fails
-- **THEN** system displays error message "La génération de la facture de frais de vie pour cette opération de mandat a échoué."
-- **AND** system shows error styling (hasError class)
-- **AND** system displays "Oui" and "Non" buttons for retry or cancel
-
-#### Scenario: Missing training departure ID
-
-- **WHEN** trainingDepartureId is undefined or null
-- **AND** user clicks "Oui" button
-- **THEN** system does not make API call
-- **AND** system handles gracefully without error
-
-## ADDED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Message Constants
-
-The system SHALL define billing generation messages as typed constants using TypeScript satisfies operator.
-
-#### Scenario: Message type safety
-
-- **WHEN** component renders
-- **THEN** messages are defined for all mutation statuses: idle, pending, success, error
-- **AND** TypeScript ensures messages match MutationStatus type
-- **AND** messages are defined as const assertions for immutability
-
-### Requirement: Activity-Based Conditional Rendering
-
-The system SHALL use Activity component for showing/hiding UI elements based on mutation state.
-
-#### Scenario: Loading state visibility
-
-- **WHEN** mutation is pending
-- **THEN** loader is visible via Activity component (mode='visible')
-- **AND** button group is hidden via Activity component (mode='hidden')
-
-#### Scenario: Action state visibility
-
-- **WHEN** mutation is not pending
-- **THEN** button group is visible via Activity component (mode='visible')
-- **AND** loader is hidden via Activity component (mode='hidden')
-
-## REMOVED Requirements

-## ADDED Requirements

-### Requirement: Explicit Named Imports for Redux Actions
-
-Files consuming Redux action modules SHALL use explicit named imports instead of namespace imports (`import * as`).
-

-- **THEN** it uses `import { list as get<Entity>List }` or `import { get as get<Entity> }` with an alias derived from the action file's entity name
-
-#### Scenario: Explicit export name

-- **THEN** it uses `import { getApniEmployee }` directly without alias

-## Why
-
-Knip v6 migrated from TypeScript's parser to oxc-parser, which no longer tracks member accesses on namespace imports (`import * as foo` → `foo.bar`) as named export usages **when the consuming file is a `.js` file**. This causes 25 false-positive "unused exports" errors when running `pnpm lint:deadcode`. Only the exports explicitly listed in that report are in scope — no other files or imports are touched.
-
-## What Changes
-
-- Replace `import * as <namespace>Actions from '...'` with explicit named imports in all consuming files
-- For generic export names (`get`, `list`): use an alias to preserve clarity (e.g. `get as getEnvelope`, `list as getBlocPathList`)
-- For explicit export names (`getApniEmployee`, `listFromTrainer`, etc.): import directly without alias
-
-## Impact
-
-- Affected specs: `import-conventions`
-- Affected code: all files consuming `src/redux/actions/*.js|ts` via namespace imports
-- No runtime behavior change — purely a static analysis compatibility fix

-## ADDED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Hook-Based Issuer List Fetching
-
-The system SHALL fetch the issuer list inside `ProvisionForm` using a TanStack `useQuery` hook (`useListIssuers`), making the form self-contained and independent of Redux state.
-
-> **Note**: The parent `ProvisionsList` fetches issuers separately via Redux for its own filter bar. The form fetch via TanStack Query is not redundant — it operates through a different cache layer. When the modal opens immediately after the list page loads, TanStack Query will serve the data from its own cache if already populated; otherwise it issues one `POST /api/legal/person/issuers` request.
-
-#### Scenario: Issuers load when modal opens

-- **WHEN** `ProvisionForm` mounts (modal opens)
-- **THEN** system sends `POST /api/legal/person/issuers` with body `{ actived: true, criteria: { size: 100 } }`
-- **AND** the "Émetteur" select is populated with `[{code}] {name}` labels once data arrives
-- **AND** while the fetch is pending the select renders with no options (form submit will be blocked by Zod `issuerId` validation)

-#### Scenario: Issuer fetch fails

-- **THEN** the "Émetteur" select renders with no options
-- **AND** no separate error UI is shown (the Zod required validation on `issuerId` prevents submission)

-The system SHALL submit provision calculation via a TanStack `useMutation` hook (`useCalculateProvision`), moving navigation out of the Redux action and into the hook.

-- **THEN** Zod validation passes
-- **AND** system sends `PUT /api/provision` with body `{ type, month: "YYYY-MM-DD", issuerId }`
-- **AND** `<LoaderOverlay loadingText="Calcul des provisions..." />` is displayed while pending
-- **AND** on success: displays toast "Les provisions ont bien été générées"

-# Proposal: Refactor ProvisionForm to Hooks-Based Architecture
-
-## Why
-
-The current `ProvisionForm` uses legacy patterns that introduce a circular import and Redux coupling:
-
-- `provision.actions.js` calls `router.navigate(...)` directly inside the `calculation` action, importing from `appRouter` and creating a circular dependency.
-- `ProvisionForm.js` is a class component wired via `reduxForm` HOC + `connect`. Form state, API loading, errors, and the issuer list all flow through Redux unnecessarily.
-- `ProvisionFormContainer.js` exists solely to glue Redux-Form + Redux connect together and can be deleted once the form owns its own data-fetching and mutation.
-- The form's own `componentDidMount` issuer fetch is redundant: `ProvisionsList` (parent) already fetches and populates `state.issuersList.items` before the modal opens. However, since we are decoupling the form entirely from Redux, the form must fetch issuers independently via `useListIssuers` — TanStack Query's cache ensures no duplicate network request occurs when both callers are active.
-
-## Scope
-
-This change is **scoped exclusively to `ProvisionForm`** and its container. The parent components (`ProvisionsList`, `ProvisionsListContainer`) are **not refactored** — only the minimum import swap in `ProvisionsList.js` is required (one line, changing the imported symbol from the old container default export to the new named component).
-
-## What Changes
-
-- **REFACTOR** `ProvisionForm.js` → `ProvisionForm.tsx`: functional component, React Hook Form + Zod validation, fully typed, named export.
-- **ADD** `src/hooks/data/issuer/useListIssuers.ts`: TanStack `useQuery` hook, `POST /api/legal/person/issuers` with `{ actived: true, criteria: { size: 100 } }`.
-- **ADD** `src/hooks/data/provision/useCalculateProvision.ts`: TanStack `useMutation` hook for `PUT /api/provision`; on success navigates via `useNavigate`, eliminating `router.navigate` from the action.
-- **ADD** `issuers` and `provisions` query keys to `src/hooks/data/queryKeys.ts`.
-- **REMOVE** `ProvisionFormContainer.js`.
-- **REMOVE** `router.navigate(...)` and `import { router }` from `provision.actions.js` `calculation` export (circular import source). The action retains its Redux dispatch logic.
-- **UPDATE** `ProvisionsList.js` (minimal): swap `import ProvisionFormContainer` for `import { ProvisionForm }` and update the JSX tag name. Prop name `closeModalCallback` is preserved on the new component to avoid any other change in the parent.
-
-## Files NOT touched
-
-- `src/components/container/ProvisionsListContainer.js`
-- `src/components/presentational/ProvisionsList/ProvisionsList.js` (beyond the one-line import swap)
-- Any other Redux reducer, saga, or action unrelated to the `calculation` circular import
-
-## Impact
-
-- **Affected specs**: `provision-form-calculation` (new spec delta)
-- **Affected code**:
-  - `src/components/presentational/ProvisionsList/ProvisionForm/ProvisionForm.js` → `.tsx`
-  - `src/components/presentational/ProvisionsList/ProvisionForm/ProvisionFormContainer.js` (deleted)
-  - `src/components/presentational/ProvisionsList/ProvisionsList.js` (import line only)
-  - `src/redux/actions/provision.actions.js` (remove `router.navigate` + its import)
-  - `src/hooks/data/queryKeys.ts`
-  - New: `src/hooks/data/issuer/useListIssuers.ts`
-  - New: `src/hooks/data/provision/useCalculateProvision.ts`
-
-## Benefits
-
-- Eliminates the circular import (`provision.actions → appRouter → ...`).
-- Removes Redux-Form from this form; form state is local.
-- Deletes a container file — net code reduction.
-- Aligns with the modern hook-based architecture (`useCreateIssuer`, `useListTrainingDepartures`, etc.).
-- `ProvisionsList` and its container remain untouched.

-# OpenSpec Instructions
-
-Instructions for AI coding assistants using OpenSpec for spec-driven development.
-
-## TL;DR Quick Checklist
-
-- Search existing work: `openspec spec list --long`, `openspec list` (use `rg` only for full-text search)
-- Decide scope: new capability vs modify existing capability
-- Pick a unique `change-id`: kebab-case, verb-led (`add-`, `update-`, `remove-`, `refactor-`)
-- Scaffold: `proposal.md`, `tasks.md`, `design.md` (only if needed), and delta specs per affected capability
-- Write deltas: use `## ADDED|MODIFIED|REMOVED|RENAMED Requirements`; include at least one `#### Scenario:` per requirement
-- Validate: `openspec validate [change-id] --strict` and fix issues
-- Request approval: Do not start implementation until proposal is approved
-
-## Three-Stage Workflow
-
-### Stage 1: Creating Changes
-
-Create proposal when you need to:
-
-- Add features or functionality
-- Make breaking changes (API, schema)
-- Change architecture or patterns
-- Optimize performance (changes behavior)
-- Update security patterns
-
-Triggers (examples):
-
-- "Help me create a change proposal"
-- "Help me plan a change"
-- "Help me create a proposal"
-- "I want to create a spec proposal"
-- "I want to create a spec"
-
-Loose matching guidance:
-
-- Contains one of: `proposal`, `change`, `spec`
-- With one of: `create`, `plan`, `make`, `start`, `help`
-
-Skip proposal for:
-
-- Bug fixes (restore intended behavior)
-- Typos, formatting, comments
-- Dependency updates (non-breaking)
-- Configuration changes
-- Tests for existing behavior
-
-**Workflow**
-
-1. Review `openspec/project.md`, `openspec list`, and `openspec list --specs` to understand current context.
-2. Choose a unique verb-led `change-id` and scaffold `proposal.md`, `tasks.md`, optional `design.md`, and spec deltas under `openspec/changes/<id>/`.
-3. Draft spec deltas using `## ADDED|MODIFIED|REMOVED Requirements` with at least one `#### Scenario:` per requirement.
-4. Run `openspec validate <id> --strict` and resolve any issues before sharing the proposal.
-
-### Stage 2: Implementing Changes
-
-Track these steps as TODOs and complete them one by one.
-
-1. **Read proposal.md** - Understand what's being built
-2. **Read design.md** (if exists) - Review technical decisions
-3. **Read tasks.md** - Get implementation checklist
-4. **Implement tasks sequentially** - Complete in order
-5. **Confirm completion** - Ensure every item in `tasks.md` is finished before updating statuses
-6. **Update checklist** - After all work is done, set every task to `- [x]` so the list reflects reality
-7. **Approval gate** - Do not start implementation until the proposal is reviewed and approved
-
-### Stage 3: Archiving Changes
-
-After deployment, create separate PR to:
-
-- Move `changes/[name]/` → `changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-[name]/`
-- Update `specs/` if capabilities changed
-- Use `openspec archive <change-id> --skip-specs --yes` for tooling-only changes (always pass the change ID explicitly)
-- Run `openspec validate --strict` to confirm the archived change passes checks
-
-## Before Any Task
-
-**Context Checklist:**
-
-- [ ] Read relevant specs in `specs/[capability]/spec.md`
-- [ ] Check pending changes in `changes/` for conflicts
-- [ ] Read `openspec/project.md` for conventions
-- [ ] Run `openspec list` to see active changes
-- [ ] Run `openspec list --specs` to see existing capabilities
-
-**Before Creating Specs:**
-
-- Always check if capability already exists
-- Prefer modifying existing specs over creating duplicates
-- Use `openspec show [spec]` to review current state
-- If request is ambiguous, ask 1–2 clarifying questions before scaffolding
-
-### Search Guidance
-
-- Enumerate specs: `openspec spec list --long` (or `--json` for scripts)
-- Enumerate changes: `openspec list` (or `openspec change list --json` - deprecated but available)
-- Show details:
-  - Spec: `openspec show <spec-id> --type spec` (use `--json` for filters)
-  - Change: `openspec show <change-id> --json --deltas-only`
-- Full-text search (use ripgrep): `rg -n "Requirement:|Scenario:" openspec/specs`
-
-## Quick Start
-
-### CLI Commands
-
-```bash
-# Essential commands
-openspec list                  # List active changes
-openspec list --specs          # List specifications
-openspec show [item]           # Display change or spec
-openspec validate [item]       # Validate changes or specs
-openspec archive <change-id> [--yes|-y]   # Archive after deployment (add --yes for non-interactive runs)
-
-# Project management
-openspec init [path]           # Initialize OpenSpec
-openspec update [path]         # Update instruction files
-
-# Interactive mode
-openspec show                  # Prompts for selection
-openspec validate              # Bulk validation mode
-
-# Debugging
-openspec show [change] --json --deltas-only
-openspec validate [change] --strict
-```
-
-### Command Flags
-
-- `--json` - Machine-readable output
-- `--type change|spec` - Disambiguate items
-- `--strict` - Comprehensive validation
-- `--no-interactive` - Disable prompts
-- `--skip-specs` - Archive without spec updates
-- `--yes`/`-y` - Skip confirmation prompts (non-interactive archive)
-
-## Directory Structure
-
-```
-openspec/
-├── project.md              # Project conventions
-├── specs/                  # Current truth - what IS built
-│   └── [capability]/       # Single focused capability
-│       ├── spec.md         # Requirements and scenarios
-│       └── design.md       # Technical patterns
-├── changes/                # Proposals - what SHOULD change
-│   ├── [change-name]/
-│   │   ├── proposal.md     # Why, what, impact
-│   │   ├── tasks.md        # Implementation checklist
-│   │   ├── design.md       # Technical decisions (optional; see criteria)
-│   │   └── specs/          # Delta changes
-│   │       └── [capability]/
-│   │           └── spec.md # ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED
-│   └── archive/            # Completed changes
-```
-
-## Creating Change Proposals
-
-### Decision Tree
-
-```
-New request?
-├─ Bug fix restoring spec behavior? → Fix directly
-├─ Typo/format/comment? → Fix directly
-├─ New feature/capability? → Create proposal
-├─ Breaking change? → Create proposal
-├─ Architecture change? → Create proposal
-└─ Unclear? → Create proposal (safer)
-```
-
-### Proposal Structure
-
-1. **Create directory:** `changes/[change-id]/` (kebab-case, verb-led, unique)
-
-2. **Write proposal.md:**
-
-```markdown
-## Why
-
-[1-2 sentences on problem/opportunity]
-
-## What Changes
-
-- [Bullet list of changes]
-- [Mark breaking changes with **BREAKING**]
-
-## Impact
-
-- Affected specs: [list capabilities]
-- Affected code: [key files/systems]
-```
-
-3. **Create spec deltas:** `specs/[capability]/spec.md`
-
-```markdown
-## ADDED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: New Feature
-
-The system SHALL provide...
-
-#### Scenario: Success case
-
-- **WHEN** user performs action
-- **THEN** expected result
-
-## MODIFIED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Existing Feature
-
-[Complete modified requirement]
-
-## REMOVED Requirements
-
-### Requirement: Old Feature
-
-**Reason**: [Why removing]
-**Migration**: [How to handle]
-```
-
-If multiple capabilities are affected, create multiple delta files under `changes/[change-id]/specs/<capability>/spec.md`—one per capability.
-
-4. **Create tasks.md:**
-
-```markdown
-## 1. Implementation
-
-- [ ] 1.1 Create database schema
-- [ ] 1.2 Implement API endpoint
-- [ ] 1.3 Add frontend component
-- [ ] 1.4 Write tests
-```
-
-5. **Create design.md when needed:**
-   Create `design.md` if any of the following apply; otherwise omit it:
-
-- Cross-cutting change (multiple services/modules) or a new architectural pattern
-- New external dependency or significant data model changes
-- Security, performance, or migration complexity
-- Ambiguity that benefits from technical decisions before coding
-
-Minimal `design.md` skeleton:
-
-```markdown
-## Context
-
-[Background, constraints, stakeholders]
-
-## Goals / Non-Goals
-
-- Goals: [...]
-- Non-Goals: [...]
-
-## Decisions
-
-- Decision: [What and why]
-- Alternatives considered: [Options + rationale]
-
-## Risks / Trade-offs
-
-- [Risk] → Mitigation
-
-## Migration Plan
-
-[Steps, rollback]
-
-## Open Questions
-
-- [...]
-```
-
-## Spec File Format
-
-### Critical: Scenario Formatting
-
-**CORRECT** (use #### headers):
-
-```markdown
-#### Scenario: User login success
-
-- **WHEN** valid credentials provided
-- **THEN** return JWT token
-```
-
-**WRONG** (don't use bullets or bold):
-
-```markdown
-- **Scenario: User login** ❌
-  **Scenario**: User login ❌
-
-### Scenario: User login ❌
-```
-
-Every requirement MUST have at least one scenario.
-
-### Requirement Wording
-
-- Use SHALL/MUST for normative requirements (avoid should/may unless intentionally non-normative)
-
-### Delta Operations
-
-- `## ADDED Requirements` - New capabilities
-- `## MODIFIED Requirements` - Changed behavior
-- `## REMOVED Requirements` - Deprecated features
-- `## RENAMED Requirements` - Name changes
-
-Headers matched with `trim(header)` - whitespace ignored.
-
-#### When to use ADDED vs MODIFIED
-
-- ADDED: Introduces a new capability or sub-capability that can stand alone as a requirement. Prefer ADDED when the change is orthogonal (e.g., adding "Slash Command Configuration") rather than altering the semantics of an existing requirement.
-- MODIFIED: Changes the behavior, scope, or acceptance criteria of an existing requirement. Always paste the full, updated requirement content (header + all scenarios). The archiver will replace the entire requirement with what you provide here; partial deltas will drop previous details.
-- RENAMED: Use when only the name changes. If you also change behavior, use RENAMED (name) plus MODIFIED (content) referencing the new name.
-
-Common pitfall: Using MODIFIED to add a new concern without including the previous text. This causes loss of detail at archive time. If you aren’t explicitly changing the existing requirement, add a new requirement under ADDED instead.
-
-Authoring a MODIFIED requirement correctly:
-
-1. Locate the existing requirement in `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`.
-2. Copy the entire requirement block (from `### Requirement: ...` through its scenarios).
-3. Paste it under `## MODIFIED Requirements` and edit to reflect the new behavior.
-4. Ensure the header text matches exactly (whitespace-insensitive) and keep at least one `#### Scenario:`.
-
-Example for RENAMED:
-
-```markdown
-## RENAMED Requirements
-
-- FROM: `### Requirement: Login`
-- TO: `### Requirement: User Authentication`
-```
-
-## Troubleshooting
-
-### Common Errors
-
-**"Change must have at least one delta"**
-
-- Check `changes/[name]/specs/` exists with .md files
-- Verify files have operation prefixes (## ADDED Requirements)
-
-**"Requirement must have at least one scenario"**
-
-- Check scenarios use `#### Scenario:` format (4 hashtags)
-- Don't use bullet points or bold for scenario headers
-
-**Silent scenario parsing failures**
-
-- Exact format required: `#### Scenario: Name`
-- Debug with: `openspec show [change] --json --deltas-only`
-
-### Validation Tips
-
-```bash
-# Always use strict mode for comprehensive checks
-openspec validate [change] --strict
-
-# Debug delta parsing
-openspec show [change] --json | jq '.deltas'
-
-# Check specific requirement
-openspec show [spec] --json -r 1
-```
-
-## Happy Path Script
-
-```bash
-# 1) Explore current state
-openspec spec list --long
-openspec list
-# Optional full-text search:
-# rg -n "Requirement:|Scenario:" openspec/specs
