-
-# 2) Choose change id and scaffold
-CHANGE=add-two-factor-auth
-mkdir -p openspec/changes/$CHANGE/{specs/auth}
-printf "## Why\n...\n\n## What Changes\n- ...\n\n## Impact\n- ...\n" > openspec/changes/$CHANGE/proposal.md
-printf "## 1. Implementation\n- [ ] 1.1 ...\n" > openspec/changes/$CHANGE/tasks.md
-
-# 3) Add deltas (example)
-cat > openspec/changes/$CHANGE/specs/auth/spec.md << 'EOF'
-## ADDED Requirements
-### Requirement: Two-Factor Authentication
-Users MUST provide a second factor during login.
-
-#### Scenario: OTP required
-- **WHEN** valid credentials are provided
-- **THEN** an OTP challenge is required
-EOF
-
-# 4) Validate
-openspec validate $CHANGE --strict
-```
-
-## Multi-Capability Example
-
-```
-openspec/changes/add-2fa-notify/
-├── proposal.md
-├── tasks.md
-└── specs/
-    ├── auth/
-    │   └── spec.md   # ADDED: Two-Factor Authentication
-    └── notifications/
-        └── spec.md   # ADDED: OTP email notification

-

-
-notifications/spec.md
-

-

-...

-
-## Best Practices
-
-### Simplicity First
-
-- Default to <100 lines of new code
-- Single-file implementations until proven insufficient
-- Avoid frameworks without clear justification
-- Choose boring, proven patterns
-
-### Complexity Triggers
-
-Only add complexity with:
-
-- Performance data showing current solution too slow
-- Concrete scale requirements (>1000 users, >100MB data)
-- Multiple proven use cases requiring abstraction
-
-### Clear References
-
-- Use `file.ts:42` format for code locations
-- Reference specs as `specs/auth/spec.md`
-- Link related changes and PRs
-
-### Capability Naming
-
-- Use verb-noun: `user-auth`, `payment-capture`
-- Single purpose per capability
-- 10-minute understandability rule
-- Split if description needs "AND"
-
-### Change ID Naming
-
-- Use kebab-case, short and descriptive: `add-two-factor-auth`
-- Prefer verb-led prefixes: `add-`, `update-`, `remove-`, `refactor-`
-- Ensure uniqueness; if taken, append `-2`, `-3`, etc.
-
-## Tool Selection Guide
-
-| Task                  | Tool | Why                      |
-| --------------------- | ---- | ------------------------ |
-| Find files by pattern | Glob | Fast pattern matching    |
-| Search code content   | Grep | Optimized regex search   |
-| Read specific files   | Read | Direct file access       |
-| Explore unknown scope | Task | Multi-step investigation |
-
-## Error Recovery
-
-### Change Conflicts
-
-1. Run `openspec list` to see active changes
-2. Check for overlapping specs
-3. Coordinate with change owners
-4. Consider combining proposals
-
-### Validation Failures
-
-1. Run with `--strict` flag
-2. Check JSON output for details
-3. Verify spec file format
-4. Ensure scenarios properly formatted
-
-### Missing Context
-
-1. Read project.md first
-2. Check related specs
-3. Review recent archives
-4. Ask for clarification
-
-## Quick Reference
-
-### Stage Indicators
-
-- `changes/` - Proposed, not yet built
-- `specs/` - Built and deployed
-- `archive/` - Completed changes
-
-### File Purposes
-
-- `proposal.md` - Why and what
-- `tasks.md` - Implementation steps
-- `design.md` - Technical decisions
-- `spec.md` - Requirements and behavior
-
-### CLI Essentials
-
-```bash

-
-Remember: Specs are truth. Changes are proposals. Keep them in sync.

-# Project Context
-
-## Purpose
-
-IPERIA's frontend application - a comprehensive React-based training management system for French home employment professionals, including childcare providers and family assistants. The application manages training sessions, certifications, and administrative tasks for the professional development of home employment workers in France.
-
-## Tech Stack
-
-- **React 19.1.1** with functional components
-- **Redux & Redux-Saga** for state management
-- **TypeScript** (mixed JS/TS codebase, migrating towards TS with strict mode)
-- **Rspack** (modern Webpack alternative) for bundling
-- **SASS/SCSS** with BEM methodology for styling
-- **Jest** with React Testing Library for testing
-- **MSW (Mock Service Worker)** for API mocking
-- **Redux-Form** for legacy forms
-- **React Hook Form** with Zod validation for new forms
-
-## Project Conventions
-
-### Code Style
-
-- **Components**: Prefer functional components with hooks over class components
-- **Functions**: Always use the `function` keyword to define all functions, including top-level components
-- **Exports**: Use named exports instead of default exports
-- **Async Code**: Use `async`/`await` for asynchronous operations
-- **TypeScript**: Write code as if TypeScript strict mode is enabled (even though it's currently disabled)
-- **CSS Naming**: Follow BEM methodology for CSS class naming
-- **CSS Units**: Use modern units (rem, vh, vw) instead of pixels for better responsiveness
-- **Stylesheets**: One SCSS file per component (when needed)
-
-### Architecture Patterns
-
-- **Directory Structure**:
-  ```
-  src/
-  ├── components/
-  │   ├── container/          # Smart components (Redux-connected) - LEGACY
-  │   ├── presentational/     # Dumb components (props only)
-  │   └── ui/                 # Reusable UI components
-  ├── redux/
-  │   ├── actions/
-  │   ├── reducers/
-  │   └── sagas/
-  ├── hooks/                  # Custom React hooks
-  ├── model/                  # TypeScript types and DTOs
-  ├── constants/              # Routes, API endpoints, etc.
-  ├── helpers/                # Utility functions
-  └── msw/                    # Mock Service Worker setup
-  ```
-- **Component Pattern Evolution**:
-  - Legacy: Container/Presentational pattern (containers connect to Redux)
-  - Modern: Prefer local state, no container, hook-based data-fetching approach for new components
-- **Form Handling**: Use React Hook Form with Zod for new forms (Redux-Form for legacy)
-
-### Testing Strategy
-
-- **Unit Tests**: Jest with React Testing Library for component testing
-- **API Mocking**: MSW for intercepting and mocking API calls
-- **Commands**:
-  - `pnpm test` - Run all tests
-  - `pnpm test --onlyChanged` - Run tests for changed files only
-  - `pnpm test -u` - Update snapshots
-- **Pre-commit Hooks**: Automatically run tests, ESLint, and Prettier before commits
-
-### Git Workflow
-
-- **Main Branch**: `develop` (not `main` or `master`)
-- **Commit Format**: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` (e.g., `fix(auth): resolve login timeout issue`)
-- **Pre-commit Hooks**: Automated checks for tests, ESLint, and Prettier
-- **Merge Requests**: Require team review before merging
-- **Common Commit Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `style`, `chore`
-
-## Domain Context
-
-### Application Purpose
-
-IPERIA is the official training management platform for French home employment professionals. It handles:
-
-- Training session registration and management
-- Professional certification tracking
-- Administrative workflows for training organizations
-- Financial aspects (funding requests, billing)
-- Progress tracking for learners
-
-### Module Status Workflow (Parcours modules/ModulePath)
-
-- `FINANCING_REQUEST` => Demande d'ouverture
-- `REJECTED_FINANCING_REQUEST` => Financement refusé
-- `AWAITING_CONTENT_VALIDATION` => En attente de validation
-- `COMMITED` => Engagé
-- `IN_PROGRESS` => En cours
-- `ENDED` => Fin de formation
-- `BILLING` => Facturé
-- `FINISHED` => Terminé
-- `CANCELLED` => Annulé
-- `SPECIFIC_TREATMENT` => Traitement spécifique
-
-## Important Constraints
-
-### Technical Constraints
-
-- **Node Version**: >= 22.12.0 (use `nvm use` with provided `.nvmrc`)
-- **Package Manager**: pnpm (not npm or yarn)
-- **HTTPS Development**: SSL certificates required for local development (runs on https://127.0.0.1:8888)
-- **TypeScript Migration**: Mixed JS/TS codebase in transition - new code should be TypeScript
-- **Browser Support**: Must support modern browsers used by training organizations
-
-### Development Environment
-
-- **Development Server**: `pnpm start` (https://127.0.0.1:8888 with hot reload)
-- **Build**: `pnpm build` for production
-- **Preview**: `pnpm preview` for HTTPS preview of built app
-- **Code Quality**: `pnpm lint` for ESLint and Stylelint checks
-
-### Architectural Constraints
-
-- Gradual migration from Redux-Form to React Hook Form
-- Moving away from Container/Presentational pattern to hooks-based approach
-- Maintaining backward compatibility during transitions
-
-## External Dependencies
-
-### Key Services & APIs
-
-- Backend API endpoints (defined in `src/constants/`)
-- Authentication services for user management
-- Training provider systems integration
-- Financial/billing systems for funding management
-
-### Development Tools
-
-- **Rspack**: Modern bundler replacing Webpack
-- **MSW**: Mock Service Worker for API simulation in development/testing
-- **Redux DevTools**: For state debugging
-- **React DevTools**: For component debugging
-
-### Documentation Resources
-
-- `.agent-os/` directory contains workflow documentation
-- OpenSpec system for change proposals and specifications
-- `CLAUDE.md` for AI assistant guidance
-- `AGENTS.md` for understanding spec format and conventions

title: fix(combobox): render label as single a11y source for accessibility and hideLabel prop to support edge cases where label need to be hidden
description:
## Why this change

  The custom combobox components exposed an `ariaLabel` prop intended to give the input an accessible name. **It never actually worked**:
  Downshift's `getLabelProps`/`getInputProps` injects an `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible `<label>`, and per the
  [accessible-name spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/accname-1.2/) `aria-labelledby` always wins over `aria-label`. So the `ariaLabel` was
  silently ignored by screen readers, and when no visible `<label>` was rendered the listbox/input pointed at a **non-existent
  element** (dangling reference).

## What changed

  - **Removed `ariaLabel`** from `ComboBoxSelect`, `ComboBoxMultiSelect`, `ComboBoxAsyncSelect`, `ComboBoxAsyncMultiSelect` and all
  the `Input*` / `Input*V2` wrappers.
  - **`label` is now required and always rendered** in the DOM, wired through Downshift's `getLabelProps()` — a single source of truth
  that correctly labels both the input *and* the dropdown listbox.
  - **Added `hideLabel`**: when a field shouldn't show a visible label (e.g. inline table cells, search inputs), the label is still
  rendered but visually hidden via the `a11y-hidden` class — so screen readers read it and `getByRole('combobox', { name })` resolves
  it.
  - Dropped the redundant `aria-label` on the inputs and made the clear/toggle button labels use `label` directly.
  - Added **`isAtLeastOneRequired`** (renders a `**` marker next to the label).

  ## Impact

  - Accessible names now work correctly for sighted-label and hidden-label fields alike; no more dangling `aria-labelledby`.
  - Cleaner, library-idiomatic labeling (let Downshift do the wiring instead of fighting it).
  - Tests query by role + accessible name instead of placeholder text, so they assert the real a11y contract.
commits: fix(combobox): update snapshot tests for combobox accessibility improvements

title: refactor(modal): [IPERIA-8597] migrate from react-modal to base-ui dialog primitives
description:
## Context
 
 Yoda Front relies on modal dialogs extensively across the application. Until now, those dialogs were powered by [`react-modal`](https://github.com/reactjs/react-modal)
 
 Beyond maintenance concerns, `react-modal` required a global `Modal.setAppElement` bootstrap call in `main.tsx` and injected its own global CSS, making it tightly coupled to the app entry point and harder to control stylistically.
 
 ## Why Base UI?
 
 [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/) is already **our UI primitives library of choice** we use it today for other components across the application. Migrating modals to Base UI's `Dialog` primitive is the natural next step: it removes our last dependency on an external modal library and consolidates all our primitive components under a single, consistent foundation.
 
 This is a two-for-one move:
 - :axe:  **Kill `react-modal`**  - an unmaintained dependency we no longer need
 - :brick: **Strengthen our Base UI adoption** - dialogs join the rest of our primitives under one roof, one API, one dependency to maintain
 
 On top of that, Base UI's `Dialog` primitive gives us:
 
 - :white_check_mark: **Full accessibility out of the box** - focus trap, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, Escape key handling - all spec-compliant by default
 - :white_check_mark: **No global setup** - no `setAppElement`, no injected CSS, no side effects on app startup
 - :white_check_mark: **Nested dialog support** - Base UI handles stacking context, backdrop layering, and scale-back animations natively
 - :white_check_mark: **Controlled & uncontrolled modes** - the new `Dialog` component supports both patterns cleanly
 - :white_check_mark: **Actively maintained** - backed by MUI with a clear roadmap and React 19 support
 ## What changed
 
 ### New `Dialog` UI component (`src/components/ui/dialog/`)
 
 A ready-to-use `Dialog` component built on top of Base UI primitives. It is titled, self-closing, and supports both controlled and uncontrolled usage. It exposes `Dialog.Close`, `Dialog.Trigger`, and `Dialog.Description` sub-components.
 
 ### `Modal` kept as a compatibility wrapper
 
 The existing `Modal` component (used in ~30 places via Redux-controlled `isOpen` / `closeHandler` pattern) now delegates to the Base UI `DialogPrimitives` internally. Its public API is **unchanged** — no call sites were broken. It is marked `@deprecated` to signal future migration toward `Dialog`.
 
 ### Migrated components
 
 Six components that had straightforward modal usage were fully migrated from `Modal` to `Dialog`:
 
 - `UserForm`
 - `FeatureFlags`
 - `InputAddressPlace` / `InputAddressPlaceV2`
 - `FundingState`, `FinancingControl`, `Payment`, `HistoryEvent`
 - `ExportsRefundingList`, `ExportsRefundingEvent`
 
 ### Removed
 
 - `react-modal` and `@types/react-modal` dependencies
 - `Modal.setAppElement` bootstrap call from `main.tsx`
 - Global react-modal CSS import from `main.scss`
 
 ## Migration path going forward
 
 Remaining usages of the legacy `Modal` wrapper should be progressively replaced with the new `Dialog` component as components are touched, following the same pattern demonstrated in this MR.






## Checklist

- [ ] re-read the JIRA to validate behavior
- [x] self-reviewed the MR (scope tight, no unrelated changes)
- [ ] wrote tests
  - [x] NO because fix some tests instead
- [ ] complex logic is documented (comment / ADR / description above)
  - [ ] NO because
- [x] manually tested both happy and error paths locally
- [x] no env-specific config hardcoded; migrations / feature flags accounted for
- [ ] screenshots added (UI changes)
  - [x] N/A

title: feat(ribFormValidationSchema): [IPERIA-8553] remove french-only iban restriction and add international iban test coverage
description:
## Context
 
 The `ribFormValidationSchema` previously enforced a hard FR-only IBAN check on the client side (`iban.getCountryCode().name === 'FR'`). Per the new spec, country-level validation moves entirely to the backend - the frontend should only verify that the IBAN is structurally parseable, and display any country rejection error returned by the API.
 
 ## What changed
 
 ### `ribFormValidationSchema`
 
 - **`ribFormSchema` refine**: replaced the `=== 'FR'` country guard with a plain `parseIban(value); return true` - valid if it parses, regardless of country.
 - **`performRibValidation`**: removed the `!== 'FR'` branch entirely; the `catch` block now only fires on a structurally invalid IBAN.
 - Both `catch` clauses drop the unused `err` binding (`catch {`) with a comment explaining the intentional empty-catch pattern (SonarQube `typescript:S2486`).
 
 ### Test coverage
 
 - **New `ribFormSchema.test.ts`**: pure unit tests covering all 7 allowed countries (FRANCE, GERMANY, SWITZERLAND, SPAIN, ITALY, MONACO, BELGIUM) via `test.each`, plus a negative case for a structurally invalid IBAN.
 - **`PaymentForm.browser.test.tsx`**: migrated two submission tests away from `vi.mock(useEditPayment)` toward real MSW interception (`worker.use(http.put(endpoints.payment, ...))`), and added a new integration test asserting a Monaco IBAN (`MC58...`) submits without a validation error.
 
 ## Removed
 
 - :axe: `vi.mock('@/hooks/data/payments/useEditPayment', { spy: true })` and its `afterEach` restore - no longer needed now that tests go through the real hook + MSW.

@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+---
+name: commit-message
+description: Suggests a commit message following the IPERIA convention. Use after staging files (git add) when the user asks for a commit message, wants help committing, or runs git commit on the current branch.
+---
+
+When suggesting a commit message:
+
+1. Run `git diff --staged` to see what is actually staged (only staged changes count - ignore unstaged/untracked files).
+2. Infer the JIRA ticket key from the current branch name or recent commits (`git log --oneline -5`). If none can be found, use `[IPERIA-XXXX]` as a literal placeholder.
+3. Propose a message following the convention below.
+
+## Convention
+
+The commit message MUST follow:
+
+```
+<type>(<scope>): [IPERIA-XXXX] <subject>
+```
+
+- **`<type>`** - one of: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `style`.
+- **`<scope>`** - the component, hook, or area touched (e.g. `useUpdateFundingState`, `Modal`, `financing-control`, `userForm`). Use the actual symbol name when the change targets one component/hook.
+- **`[IPERIA-XXXX]`** - the JIRA ticket key. If no ticket is provided, write `[IPERIA-XXXX]` literally as a placeholder.
+- **`<subject>`** - short, lowercase, imperative mood ("migrate", "add", "prevent", "move"), no trailing period.
+
+Examples:
+
+```
+feat(APNI-financing-control): [IPERIA-8579] implement financing control workflow and Tag for public market ModulePath
+refactor(Modal): [IPERIA-8597] migrate from Modal to Dialog in FeatureFlags component
+```

+---
+name: pr-description
+description: Writes pull request descriptions in GitLab-flavored markdown, ready to paste into a merge request. Use when creating a PR/MR, writing a PR, or when the user asks to summarize changes for a pull request.
+---
+
+When writing a PR description:
+
+1. Run `git diff develop...HEAD` (and `git log develop..HEAD --oneline`) to see all changes on this branch.
+2. Output **GitLab-flavored markdown**, ready to paste directly into a merge request. **Always wrap the entire output in a fenced code block (` ```markdown `) so the raw markdown is visible and copy-pasteable.**
+3. Follow the structure below, scaling it to the PR's scope - a small fix only needs Context + What changed; a large migration uses every section.
+
+## Title
+
+The PR title follows the commit message convention - see the `commit-message` skill.
+
+## Section structure
+
+### `## Context`
+
+Set the scene: what the code looked like before and what problem/limitation motivated the change. Link to relevant libraries/docs with markdown links.
+
+### `## Why <approach>` (optional)
+
+When the PR chooses a specific approach or library, justify it. Use a sub-heading naming the choice (e.g. `## Why Base UI?`). Bullet the concrete wins.
+
+### `## What changed`
+
+The core section. Group changes under `###` sub-headings by area (new component, refactored module, compatibility wrapper, etc.). Describe behavior and public-API impact, not a file-by-file dump.
+
+### `## Removed` (optional)
+
+List deleted dependencies, files, bootstrap calls, or config when the PR removes things.
+
+### `## Migration path going forward` (optional)
+
+When the PR is one step of a larger effort, state what remains and the pattern to follow.
+
+## Formatting conventions
+
+- Use GitLab emoji shortcodes for emphasis where they aid scanning - e.g. `:white_check_mark:` for benefits, `:axe:` for removals, `:brick:` for foundational wins. Keep them purposeful, not decorative.
+- **Bold** the key noun in each bullet so the list scans quickly.
+- Use markdown links for external references (libraries, docs, tickets).
+- Wrap code symbols, paths, and component names in backticks.

+import type { BillingSettingsInput } from '@/model/SettingsInput';
+import type {
+  BillingSettingFormData,
+  FunderTrainingFormData,
+} from './billingSettingsValidationSchema';
+import type { FundersFormattedDTO } from '@/model/FunderDTO';
+
+export function formatBillingSettingsFormData(
+  values: BillingSettingFormData,
+  fundersFormatted: FundersFormattedDTO,
+): BillingSettingsInput {
+  const settingsInput: BillingSettingsInput = {
+    DISPLAY_PAID_BILL_INFORMATION: [{ value: values.displayPaidDateInput }],
+    GROUP_THRESHOLD_SPE_PLAN: [{ value: values.groupThresholdSpe }],
+    GROUP_THRESHOLD_ASSMAT_PLAN: [{ value: values.groupThresholdAssmat }],
+    MODULE_PATH_BILLING_PLAN_SPE_THRESHOLD: [{ value: values.ceilingSpe }],
+    MODULE_PATH_BILLING_PLAN_ASSMAT_THRESHOLD: [{ value: values.ceilingAssmat }],
+    MODULE_PATH_BILLING_PLAN_THRESHOLD: [{ value: values.ceilingGlobal }],
+    AMOUNT_OF_ALLOWANCE_ASS_MAT: values.assmatAllowances,
+    AMOUNT_OF_ALLOWANCE_SPE: values.speAllowances,
+    THRESHOLD_CESU_SPE: values.thresholdCesuSpe,
+    THRESHOLD_URSSAF_SPE: values.thresholdUrssafSpe,
+    THRESHOLD_PAJEMPLOI_SPE: values.thresholdPajemploiSpe,
+    THRESHOLD_PAJEMPLOI_ASS_MAT: values.thresholdPajemploiAssmat,
+    FUNDER_LIVING_COST_ASSMAT: _mapFundersWithName(
+      values.funderLivingCostAssmat,
+      fundersFormatted.ASSMAT_PLAN,
+    ),
+    FUNDER_LIVING_COST_SPE: _mapFundersWithName(
+      values.funderLivingCostSpe,
+      fundersFormatted.SPE_PLAN,
+    ),
+    FUNDER_TRAINING_SPE_PLAN: _mapFundersWithName(
+      values.funderTrainingSpePlan,
+      fundersFormatted.SPE_PLAN,
+    ),
+    FUNDER_TRAINING_SPE_CPF: _mapFundersWithName(
+      values.funderTrainingSpeCpf,
+      fundersFormatted.SPE_CPF,
+    ),
+    FUNDER_TRAINING_ASSMAT_PLAN: _mapFundersWithName(
+      values.funderTrainingAssmatPlan,
+      fundersFormatted.ASSMAT_PLAN,
+    ),
+    FUNDER_TRAINING_ASSMAT_CPF: _mapFundersWithName(
+      values.funderTrainingAssmatCpf,
+      fundersFormatted.ASSMAT_CPF,
+    ),
+    PEDAGOGIC_COSTS_BILLING_YEAR: [
+      {
+        value: values.pedagogicCostsBillingYear || '',
+      },
+    ],
+    LIVING_COSTS_BILLING_YEAR: [
+      {
+        value: values.livingCostsBillingYear || '',
+      },
+    ],
+    LIVING_COSTS_BILLING: [
+      {
+        value: values.livingCostsBilling,
+      },
+    ],
+    ISSUER_PEDAGOGIC_EXPENSES_COST: values.issuerPedagogicExpensesCost.map((field) => ({
+      name: field.issuer.value,
+      value: field.template.value,
+      startDate: field.startDate,
+      endDate: field.endDate,
+    })),
+    ISSUER_LIVING_COST: values.issuerLivingCost.map((field) => ({
+      name: field.issuer.value,
+      value: field.template.value,
+      startDate: field.startDate,
+      endDate: field.endDate,
+    })),
+    ADMINISTRATIVE_FEE: values.administrativeFee,
+  };
+
+  return settingsInput;
+}
+
+function _mapFundersWithName(
+  values: FunderTrainingFormData[],
+  source: FundersFormattedDTO[keyof FundersFormattedDTO],
+) {
+  return values.map((funder) => ({
+    value: funder.value,
+    name: source.find((funderFormatted) => funderFormatted.id === funder.value)?.name,
+    startDate: funder.startDate,
+    endDate: funder.endDate,
+  }));
+}

+type SettingsKeyWithDateValue = {

+}[keyof SettingsDTO];
+
+export function initializeOpeningRequestSettingsFormData(
+  settingsData: SettingsParams,
+): OpeningRequestSettingFormData {
+  const settings = settingsData.content;
+
+  const maxDaysFundingRequestDelayAssmat =
+    settings?.MAXIMUM_DAYS_TO_VALIDATE_ASSMAT_FINANCING_REQUEST?.at(0)?.value ?? '';
+  const maxDaysFundingRequestDelaySpe =
+    settings?.MAXIMUM_DAYS_TO_VALIDATE_SPE_FINANCING_REQUEST?.at(0)?.value ?? '';

+    settings?.ASSMAT_AUTOMATIC_VALIDATION_DATE?.at(0)?.value ?? '';

+  const modulePathMaxDays = settings?.MODULE_PATH_MAX_DAYS?.at(0)?.value ?? '';
+  const daysBeforeFirstMailNotification =
+    settings?.DAYS_BEFORE_FIRST_MAIL_NOTIFICATION?.at(0)?.value ?? '';
+  const daysBeforeNewMailNotification =
+    settings?.DAYS_BEFORE_NEW_MAIL_NOTIFICATION?.at(0)?.value ?? '';
+  const automaticCancellation = settings?.AUTOMATIC_CANCELLATION?.at(0)?.value ?? '';
+
+  function getAverageCost(field: SettingsKeyWithDateValue) {
+    const financingRequestAverageCost = settings?.[field] ?? [];
+
+    return financingRequestAverageCost.map(
+      (item) =>
+        ({
+          value: item.value,
+          startDate: item.startDate ?? '',
+          endDate: item.endDate ?? '',
+        }) satisfies AverageCostFormData[number],
+    );
+  }
+
+  return {
+    maxDaysFundingRequestDelayAssmat,

+    doAeAssmatLivingCost: getAverageCost('DO_AE_ASSMAT_LIVING_COST'),
+    doAeSpeLivingCost: getAverageCost('DO_AE_SPE_LIVING_COST'),
+    doAeAssmatAverageAllocationCost: getAverageCost('DO_AE_ASSMAT_AVERAGE_ALLOCATION_COST'),
+    doAeSpeAverageAllocationCost: getAverageCost('DO_AE_SPE_AVERAGE_ALLOCATION_COST'),
+    doAeSpeAverageSalaryCost: getAverageCost('DO_AE_SPE_AVERAGE_SALARY_COST'),
+  } satisfies OpeningRequestSettingFormData;
+}

title: refactor(addressUtils): [IPERIA-8644] extract formatAddressIds helper and reuse across form formatters
description:
## Context

Several form formatters (`MandataryForm`, `OfEmployeeForm`, `TrainingAgencyForm`, `UserForm`) each duplicated the same logic to turn an `InputAddressPlaceV2` address value into the `addresseIds` / `googlePlaceIds` / `guriIds` arrays expected by `PhysicalPersonInput`. The same three-line dance was copy-pasted everywhere, and `UserFormFinalValues` still typed its `address` as the legacy `AddressInput`.

## What changed

### New `formatAddressIds` helper

- **Centralized** the addressId formatting from `InputAddressPlaceV2` into a single `formatAddressIds` helper in `addressUtils`.
- **Reused** it across `MandataryForm`, `OfEmployeeForm`, `TrainingAgencyForm`, `UserForm` (`formatUserInput`), and `useUserCreationFlow`, removing the duplicated inline logic.
- **Added** unit tests covering the common single-ids, and `null`/`undefined` address.

### Type alignment

- **Updated** `UserFormFinalValues` to use `ContactFormData['address']` instead of the legacy `AddressInput` by default.
- Added **temporary reconversions** in `UserForm`, `UserAccountForm`, and `useUserCreationFlow` to keep the still-redux-form employee flows working until they are migrated.

## Migration path going forward

The temporary reconversions (TODO-flagged) will be removed once `UserAccountForm` is fully migrated away from redux-form.

files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+---
+name: jira-ticket-description
+description: Writes or updates a JIRA ticket description (in French) summarizing work done on the current branch. Use when the user asks to document a ticket, write up what was done, or fill in a JIRA description from their changes.
+---
+
+Write a French JIRA ticket **description** summarizing the work done, then update the ticket.
+
+> ⚠️ **The output goes in the ticket's `description` field — NEVER in a comment.** Use `jira_update_issue`, never `jira_add_comment`. This is the single most important rule of this skill; do not add or update a comment unless the user explicitly and specifically asks for one.
+
+## Workflow
+
+1. **Identify the ticket key** (`IPERIA-XXXX`), in this priority order:
+   - If the user gave a key or a Jira link in their prompt, use it. Extract the key from a URL like `.../browse/IPERIA-8649` (match `IPERIA-\d+`).
+   - Otherwise, derive it from the current branch name if it matches `.../IPERIA-XXXX...` (e.g. `fix/IPERIA-8649`, `refactor/IPERIA-8638-1`). Get the branch with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.
+   - Otherwise (e.g. branch `chore/rspack-react-deps` has no key), ask the user for the ticket key or link before continuing. Do not guess.
+2. **Gather the real changes** — never guess from memory:
+   - `git log develop..HEAD --pretty=format:'%h %s'`
+   - `git diff develop...HEAD --stat`
+   - Read the key before/after files (use `git show develop:<path>` for the old version) so the write-up describes what _actually_ changed.
+3. **Fetch the ticket** with `mcp__atlassian-ekino__jira_get_issue` (using the key from step 1, fields `summary,description,status`) to get its current state.
+   - If the fetch fails or returns no ticket (wrong or mistyped key, ticket in another project, deleted), stop and tell the user the key could not be found, then ask them to confirm or correct it before continuing.
+   - Never fall back to another ticket or invent one.
+   - Once fetched, show the user the ticket key and its `summary` so they can catch a wrong-ticket mistake before anything is written.
+4. **Draft the description in French**, in the structure below, wrapped in a fenced code block so the raw markup is visible.
+5. **Confirm with the user** before writing. Only after approval, call `mcp__atlassian-ekino__jira_update_issue` with `{"description": "..."}` — i.e. write to the **description field**, not a comment.
+
+## Critical rules (learned the hard way)
+
+- **Write Jira wiki markup, NOT Markdown.** The Atlassian MCP mangles Markdown: `*bold*` becomes literal `\*`, and `<button>`, `+`, etc. get dropped. Use:
+  - Headers: `h2.`, `h3.`
+  - Bullets: lines starting with `* `
+  - Code/identifiers: `{{SettingsForm}}`
+  - Avoid raw `<...>` angle brackets, leading `+`, and Markdown `**bold**`/`### headers`.
+
+## Structure
+
+Follow the team convention — **Contexte / Objectif ou Problème observé / Tâche / Impact** — scaling sections to scope:
+
+```
+h2. Contexte
+<what the code looked like before, the legacy patterns / problem motivating the change, and the goal>
+
+h2. Objectif ou Problème observé
+<choose the framing that matches the nature of the work and rename the heading to just one of the two:
+- h2. Objectif — for a technical task or improvement: state the concrete goal the work aims to reach (e.g. migrate a form to RHF, extract a shared helper) and why it is worth doing.
+- h2. Problème observé — for a bug or defect: describe the observed symptom, when it happens, and its consequence for users/devs. This is what motivates and scopes the fix that follows in Tâche.>
+
+h2. Tâche
+<what was done, grouped under h3. sub-headings by area; describe behavior and public-API impact, not a file-by-file dump>
+
+h2. Impact
+<what this changes for users/devs: removed dependencies, deleted files, migration path, breaking changes>
+
+```
+
+If part of a larger effort, add a `h2. Reste à faire` section stating what remains and the pattern to follow.

title: refactor(api-tree-architecture): [IPERIA-8658] introduce src/api layer and break the transport <--> error-presentation circular import
description:
#### Highlight: Non-critical circular imports reduced from 255 to 125! :tada:

## Context

The HTTP transport and TanStack Query setup were scattered and mislabelled:

- `fetcher`, `blobFetcher`, `HttpVerb`, `getRequestHeaders`, `UNAUTHORIZED_ERROR`, `STALE_TIME`, the `queryClient` instance and `QUERY_KEYS` all lived inside **`src/hooks/data/queryClient.ts`** — a single "god" module that every data hook pulled in wholesale.
- Error formatting lived in `src/helpers/api.tsx` + `src/helpers/http.ts`, and the error templates in `src/constants/errors`.

Because `fetcher` sat under `hooks/data/`, it read like a hook — and that mislabelling let a **circular import** quietly form:

fetcher → http → getApiErrorMessages → apiErrorTemplates
        → LinkedTrainingAgenciesErrorMessage → getIsAuthenticatedCache → queryClient/fetcher

In other words, the **lowest layer (transport) depended transitively on the highest layer** (React error presentation + a data hook), which depended back on transport. ES modules load the whole module on import, so this was a real cycle, not just a type-level one — it surfaced as fragile import-order bugs.

## Why this structure

A dedicated **`src/api`** layer with a single hard rule: **dependencies only ever point downward.**

components / hooks/data  →  src/api/*  →  model / enums / constants / helpers-utils / components-ui

- :brick: **`src/api` is the floor** — it never imports `@/hooks/**` or `@/components/{presentational,container}/**`. The only upward edge allowed is `src/api → @/components/ui/*` (pure, leaf UI).
- :white_check_mark: **The cycle becomes structurally impossible**, not just currently-absent.
- :white_check_mark: **`fetcher` is no longer mislabelled** as a hook — it's plain transport, in a folder that says so.

## What changed

### New `src/api` layer final tree

```
src/api/
├── authentication/
│   └── isAuthenticatedCache.ts          # leaf → queryClient + queryKeys + DTO type (no fetcher)
├── errors/
│   ├── apiErrorCodes.ts
│   ├── apiErrorMessages.ts
│   ├── apiErrorTemplates.tsx
│   ├── constant.ts                       # GENERIC_API_ERROR_MESSAGES
│   ├── getApiErrorMessages.tsx           # ← from helpers/api.tsx
│   ├── types.ts
│   └── components/
│       ├── LinkedTrainingAgenciesErrorMessage.tsx
│       ├── _LinkedTrainingAgenciesErrorMessage.scss
│       └── PaymentStatusNotValidError.tsx
├── http/
│   ├── httpVerb.ts                        # enum — leaf, zero imports
│   ├── constants.ts                       # UNAUTHORIZED_ERROR
│   ├── headers.ts                         # getRequestHeaders
│   ├── types.ts                           # FetcherInitParams, BlobFetcherError, RequestInitParams
│   ├── fetcher.ts
│   ├── blobFetcher.ts
│   ├── getFallbackErrorMessage.ts         # ← from helpers/utils/errorHelpers.ts
│   └── getApiErrorFromHttpResponse.ts     # ← from helpers/http.ts
└── queryClient/
    ├── queryClient.ts                     # createQueryClient + instance (leaf)
    ├── queryKeys.ts                       # ← from hooks/data/queryKeys.ts
    └── staleTime.ts                       # STALE_TIME

```

### Split the "god" queryClient.ts

The **`queryClient` instance is now a leaf** — it imports only `QUERY_KEYS` + `UNAUTHORIZED_ERROR`, no longer `fetcher`. Transport functions and constants moved to their own files. Data hooks no longer drag the entire HTTP/error stack in just to read a `STALE_TIME`.

### Broke the circular import

- **Cache accessors extracted** (`getIsAuthenticatedCache`, `setIsAuthenticatedCache`, …) out of the `useGetIsAuthenticated` hook into **`src/api/authentication/isAuthenticatedCache.ts`** — a leaf that depends only on the `queryClient` instance + `QUERY_KEYS`, never on `fetcher`.
- **`LinkedTrainingAgenciesErrorMessage`** now imports that leaf. It stays **hook-free on purpose** — it's rendered by the non-React `API_ERROR_TEMPLATES` map, so it reads the cache imperatively (documented in-code) rather than via `useQuery`.
- **`MessageLink`** removed (it's a pure UI leaf wrapping `Link`) and directly use the facade `Link` so the sole upward dependency from `src/api` is the allowed `→ components/ui` edge, exception-free.

### Import repoints

~**328 files** repointed to the new `@/api/*` paths — data hooks (`src/hooks`, 156), legacy Redux reducers/actions (`src/redux`, 113), services, MSW handlers, and test utilities. No behavior change: pure move + re-import.

## Removed

- :axe: **`src/hooks/data/queryClient.ts`** — the god module, split across `src/api/{http,queryClient}`.
- :axe: **`src/components/presentational/common/Messages/MessageLink/`** — directly use `Link` from `components/ui`.
- Old homes emptied via renames: `src/constants/errors/*`, `src/helpers/api.tsx`, `src/helpers/utils/errorHelpers.ts`, `src/hooks/data/queryKeys.ts`.

### Note and migration path going forward

Legacy `src/helpers/http.ts` keeps only deprecated method such as the untouched RSAA / redux-thunk helpers (`getCallAPIAction`, `rawHttpRequest`, `callApiActionFromAsyncThunk`).

title: test(useAuthenticationFlow): [IPERIA-8680/IPERIA-8681] reproduce the shared query meta race in the auth redux sync test
description:
## Context

The `ab821b0c8` fix (IPERIA-8680 / IPERIA-8681) replaced the `meta.onSuccess` / `meta.onError` callbacks of `useGetIsAuthenticated` with local effects in `useAuthenticationFlow`. The regression test added at the time did assert that Redux gets populated from the auth query, but it **also passed against the old implementation**: it did not reproduce the race that caused the bug.

Reason: on mount, React runs child effects before the parent's. `AppLayout` therefore wrote its `meta` last, and the callback was still there when the response landed. Without another observer re-rendering while the request is in flight, there is nothing to detect.

## What changed

### Control over when the response lands

The MSW handler for `/isAuthenticated` now awaits a promise (`authResponseGate`) whose `resolve` is exposed to the test. The request stays `pending` until the test releases it: no `setTimeout`, no approximate timing window.

### Simulating another observer of the same `queryKey`

New custom component test `PermissionObserverPage` (`/permission-observer`) calling `usePermission`, like other call sites across the app. A button lets the test re-render it on demand.

That re-render is the whole point: [`useBaseQuery`](https://github.com/TanStack/query/blob/main/packages/react-query/src/useBaseQuery.ts) calls `observer.setOptions(defaultedOptions)` in a `useEffect` on **every** render, which triggers `query.setOptions()` and fully replaces the query's shared options, `meta` included.

### Sequence the test now forces

1. Mount: `AppLayout` writes its `meta` last, with the callback
2. `GET /isAuthenticated` fires and blocks on the gate
3. Button click: `meta` is rewritten without the callback, and nothing restores it
4. Response released: `QueryCache.onSuccess` reads `meta.onSuccess === undefined`

:white_check_mark: **Fails** against the pre-fix implementation (`login.id` stays empty)
:white_check_mark: **Passes** with the fix, since the local effect on `data` no longer depends on a shared channel

+- Write components as functions, using the `function` keyword and named exports. Class components and `PureComponent` are no longer used.
 
 ### Redux
 
-- Reducers, actions and sagas are located into the folders `redux/reducers`, `redux/actions` and `redux/sagas`.
+- The store is built with [Redux Toolkit](https://redux-toolkit.js.org/), configured in `redux/store.ts`. Slices, actions and middleware live in `redux/reducers`, `redux/actions` and `redux/middleware`.
+
+- **Redux is considered legacy here.** Don't add state to it for new features: server state belongs in [TanStack Query](https://tanstack.com/query/latest), and everything else in local component state. Existing Redux state is progressively migrated the same way.
 
-- Use Redux `connect` only into React container modules.
+- `connect` is legacy too, and only tolerated in the container components that already use it. Reach for the typed hooks in new code.
 
 ### CSS/SASS
 
-- All scss files should be into "presentational" components folders.
+- Keep one `.scss` file per component, next to it, and only if the component needs one. Common could shared behaviors.
 
-- Use 1 scss files for each component. Common could shared behaviors.
+- Class names should respect [BEM](http://getbem.com/naming/).
 
-- Modules should respect [BEM](http://getbem.com/naming/) class naming.
+- Prefer relative units (`rem`, `vh`, `vw`). Use `px` where precision matters: borders, shadows, radii, SVG sizing and small alignment tweaks.
 
 ### Rspack
 
 2 rspack configs are available :
 
-- `config/rspack.config.local.js` : For local development.
+- `config/rspack.config.local.js` : for local development, picked when `NODE_ENV=dev_local` (what `pnpm start` sets).
 
-- `config/rspack.config.prod.js` : For production environment (dev, staging, production) deployment`.
+- `config/rspack.config.prod.js` : for every deployed environment, picked when `NODE_ENV=production` and used as the fallback for any other value.
 
-The right one is automatically picked based on the value of the `NODE_ENV` environment variable.
+The mapping lives in `rspack.config.js` at the root.
 
 ### Testing
 
-- Always test presentational components with at least a snapshot.
+- Test files are named `<file>.test.ts`/`<file>.test.tsx` and placed under a `__tests__` directory. Two suffixes select a specific Vitest project: `<file>.browser.test.tsx` for Browser Mode, and `<file>.isolated.test.tsx` for tests needing a clean environment.
 
-- Every test file should be named `<file>.test.js` and be placed under a `__tests__` directory.
+- Assert on behaviour rather than on rendered markup. Snapshots are legacy: the existing ones are being removed, so don't add new ones.
 
 ### Git
 
-- A hook executing **unit tests**, **SassLint** and **ESLint** and **Prettier** is plugged before the push.
+- A **pre-commit** hook runs `lint-staged` (oxlint, oxfmt and stylelint on staged files) followed by the tests affected by your changes.
 
 - Don't commit directly to `develop` branch. Always use a merge request with your feature branch.

description:

- [x] self-reviewed the MR (scope tight, no unrelated changes)
- [ ] wrote tests
  - [x] NO because
- [ ] complex logic is documented (comment / ADR / description above)
  - [x] NO because
- [x] manually tested both happy and error paths locally
- [x] no env-specific config hardcoded; migrations / feature flags accounted for
- [ ] screenshots added (UI changes)
  - [x] N/A

title: fix(parseDateValue): [IPERIA-8676] handle year-month format for Firefox compatibility in exportedDate column
description:
## Context

`parseDateValue` fell back to the native `new Date(value)` constructor when a value wasn't in one of the explicitly handled formats. 

The `exportedDate` column in `ExportsCegidList` uses a `yyyy-M`/`yyyy-MM` (non-padded month) value, which is not valid ISO 8601. Parsing of such non-standard strings via `new Date()` is **engine-dependent**: Chrome accepts it, Firefox returns an `Invalid Date`, breaking the column display for Firefox users.

## What changed

### `parseDateValue`
- Added an explicit check for the `yyyy-M`/`yyyy-MM` pattern, parsed with `date-fns`'s `parse` and a new `DateFormat.YEAR_MONTH` (`yyyy-M`) format instead of relying on the native `Date` constructor fallback.

### Tests
- Added coverage for `parseDateValue` and `toFullMonthYear` with non-padded (`2026-9`) and padded (`2024-06`) year-month values.
commits: fix(parseDateValue): [IPERIA-8676] handle year-month format for Firefox compatibility in exportedDate column

+import type { FunderFormData } from './funderFormValidationSchema';
+import type { FunderInput } from '@/model/FunderInput';
+import { formatAddressIds } from '@/helpers/utils/addressUtils';
+
+export function formatFunderFormData(values: FunderFormData): FunderInput {
+  const { addresseIds, googlePlaceIds, guriIds } = formatAddressIds(values.address);
+
+  const isOngoingTraining = values.type === 'ONGOING_TRAINING';
+
+  return {
+    cegid: values.cegid || null,
+    type: values.type,
+    branch: isOngoingTraining ? values.branch : null,
+    mode: isOngoingTraining ? values.mode : null,
+    apniDematerialization: isOngoingTraining ? (values.apniDematerialization ?? false) : false,
+    legalPersonInput: {
+      actived: true,
+      id: values.legalPersonId,
+      name: values.name,
+      extraName: values.extraName || null,
+      // For an unknown reason, the legacy formatLegalPersonInput stripped the protocol
+      // and rebuilt it on the Funder card. Why not just send the full URL and retrieve it
+      // as-is to avoid this unnecessary transformation complexity ?
+      website: values.website ? values.website.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '') : null,
+      mobileNumber: values.mobileNumber || null,
+      fixNumber: values.fixNumber || null,
+      faxNumber: values.faxNumber || null,
+      mail: values.mail,
+      addresseIds,
+      complementAddress: {
+        addressId: addresseIds?.at(0) ?? null,
+        complement: values.complementAddress || null,
+      },
+      googlePlaceIds,
+      guriIds,
+    },
+  };
+}

+import { z } from 'zod';
+
+import { baseContactSchema } from '@/helpers/validations/schemas/baseContactSchema';
+import { FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES } from '@/constants/formErrorMessages';
+import { isInvalidURL } from '@/helpers/utils/stringUtils';
+
+export type FunderFormData = z.infer<typeof funderFormValidationSchema>;
+
+const baseFunderFormSchema = z.object({
+  ...baseContactSchema.shape,
+  name: z.string().min(1, { error: FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.funder.nameRequired }),
+  extraName: z.string().nullable().optional(),
+  cegid: z.string().nullable().optional(),
+  apniDematerialization: z.boolean().nullable().optional(),
+  website: z
+    .string()
+    .nullable()
+    .optional()
+    .refine((url) => !url || !isInvalidURL(url), { error: FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.url.invalid }),
+  /**
+   * Legacy internal fields, never displayed, only present when editing an existing funder.
+   */
+  legalPersonId: z.string().optional(),
+});
+
+export const funderFormValidationSchema = z.discriminatedUnion(
+  'type',
+  [
+    baseFunderFormSchema.extend({
+      type: z.literal('CERTIFICATION'),
+    }),
+    baseFunderFormSchema.extend({
+      type: z.literal('ONGOING_TRAINING'),
+      branch: z.enum(['ASSMAT', 'SPE', 'DE', 'SHB', 'NA'], {
+        error: FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.funder.branchRequired,
+      }),
+      mode: z.enum(['PLAN', 'CPF', 'NA'], { error: FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.funder.modeRequired }),
+    }),
+  ],
+  { error: FORM_ERROR_MESSAGES.funder.typeRequired },
+);

files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+/**
+ * Minimal PDF with a single page of visible text, used to exercise the real react-pdf
+ * rendering pipeline in tests without shipping a binary fixture file.
+ *
+ * The xref table below is intentionally approximate: pdf.js falls back to scanning the
+ * file for `obj` markers when the xref offsets don't resolve, so exact byte counting
+ * isn't required to keep this fixture parseable.
+ */
+export const PDF_SAMPLE_TEXT = 'Hello from PDF hell...';
+
+export function pdfSampleMock(): ArrayBuffer {
+  const contentStream = `BT /F1 24 Tf 20 150 Td (${PDF_SAMPLE_TEXT}) Tj ET`;
+
+  const source = `%PDF-1.4
+    1 0 obj<</Type/Catalog/Pages 2 0 R>>endobj
+    2 0 obj<</Type/Pages/Kids[3 0 R]/Count 1>>endobj
+    3 0 obj<</Type/Page/Parent 2 0 R/MediaBox[0 0 300 200]/Resources<</Font<</F1 4 0 R>>>>/Contents 5 0 R>>endobj
+    4 0 obj<</Type/Font/Subtype/Type1/BaseFont/Helvetica>>endobj
+    5 0 obj<</Length ${contentStream.length}>>
+    stream
+    ${contentStream}
+    endstream
+    endobj
+    xref
+    0 6
+    0000000000 65535 f
+    0000000000 00000 n
+    0000000000 00000 n
+    0000000000 00000 n
+    0000000000 00000 n
+    0000000000 00000 n
+    trailer<</Size 6/Root 1 0 R>>
+    startxref
+    0
+    %%EOF`;
+
+  return new TextEncoder().encode(source).buffer;
+}

title: refactor(legacyApiMiddleware): [IPERIA-8726] migrate away from redux-api-middleware to custom middleware
description:
## Context

The Redux store relied on the third-party [`redux-api-middleware`](https://github.com/agraboso/redux-api-middleware) (RSAA) to dispatch the legacy API call actions created by `getCallAPIAction` (`helpers/http.ts`). The package is unmaintained, forced `serializableCheck` to be disabled across the **entire** store, and required type casts working around RTK's typing (`apiMiddleware as Middleware<{}, ...>`).

## Why a custom middleware?

- **No unmaintained dependency**: `redux-api-middleware` and its `@types` package are dropped entirely.
- **Same contract, smaller surface**: `legacyApiMiddleware` reproduces exactly the request/success/error dispatch behavior existing legacy reducers depend on, so no call site (`getCallAPIAction` usages) needs to change.
- **Restores type safety**: replaces the RSAA-derived types (`RSAAAction`, `RSAACall`) with explicit types (`LegacyApiCall`, `LegacyApiErrorPayload`, request/success/error descriptors) that match what the middleware actually does.
- **Narrower `serializableCheck` exemption**: instead of disabling it store-wide, only `meta.nextSideEffect` and `meta.nextActionDispatch` action paths are ignored, since they're the only ones still carrying functions/whole actions for `listenerMiddleware`.

## What changed

### New middleware
- Added `src/redux/middleware/legacyApiMiddleware.ts`: intercepts actions carrying the internal `LEGACY_API_CALL` key, performs the `fetch`, then dispatches the request action (synchronously unless its `payload`/`meta` is a resolver function), followed by the success or error action based on the response.
- Handles network errors (`RequestError`), internal resolver errors (`InternalError`), and HTTP errors (`ApiError`) with distinct payload shapes.
- Prepended to the store (`.prepend(legacyApiMiddleware)`), ahead of `listenerMiddleware`.

### `getCallAPIAction` facade (`src/helpers/http.ts`)
- Swapped the `RSAA` key for `LEGACY_API_CALL`.
- Extracted the default success/error payload resolvers (`getSuccessPayloadResolver`, `resolveErrorPayload`) and a `_getJSON` helper handling bodyless responses (204/205 statuses, non-JSON content-type).

### Types (`src/helpers/reduxCustomTypes.ts`)
- Removed `redux-api-middleware` type imports (`RSAAAction`, `RSAACall`).
- Added `LegacyApiCall`, `LegacyApiErrorPayload`, and the `RequestTypeDescriptor`/`SuccessTypeDescriptor`/`ErrorTypeDescriptor` types matching the new middleware's contract.

### Store (`src/redux/store.ts`)
- Replaced `apiMiddleware` with `legacyApiMiddleware`.
- Scoped `serializableCheck` to ignore only the two legacy action paths instead of disabling it entirely.

### Tests
- Added `src/helpers/__tests__/getCallAPIAction.test.ts` covering the facade and its resolvers.
- Updated `src/helpers/__tests__/http.test.ts` and `src/test/test-utils/testSetupStore.ts` accordingly.

## Removed

- :axe: `redux-api-middleware` and `@types/redux-api-middleware` from `package.json`/lockfile.
- :axe: Renovate freeze rule entries for both packages (`.gitlab/renovate.json`).

## Migration path going forward

- `getCallAPIAction` / `legacyApiMiddleware` remain a bridge for legacy Redux data fetching. New code should keep using TanStack Query with `fetcher` instead.
- `immutableCheck` is still disabled on the store — a follow-up ticket should look for state mutations before re-enabling it.

description:

- Remove `treatJsFilesAsJsx` custom plugin and esbuild dependency
- Switch from `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc` to `@vitejs/plugin-react` plugin

### Plugin swap to follow Vitest recommandation for our case...

| Plugin           | CI test run time |
|------------------|-------------------|
| Old (SWC plugin) | ~250-265 sec      |
| New              | ~256-262 sec    |

title: refactor(ItinerarySynthesis): [IPERIA-8730] remove dead OpenLayers/guri code path and migrate direction fetching to Tanstack Query
description:
## Context

`ItinerarySynthesis` (the itinerary/access plan shown from `TrainingDeparture` and `EvaluationDeparture`) embedded two map implementations: an OpenLayers (`ol`) map fed by the backend's `guri` endpoint, and a Google Maps implementation.

The OpenLayers branch was actually dead code: the `openLayer` flag was always `false` and `directionsGuri` always stayed empty/`undefined`, so only the Google Maps view ever rendered. The entire associated Redux chain (container, action, reducer, endpoint) served no purpose.

The component also relied on the legacy container/presentational pattern (`ItinerarySynthesisContainer.js`) and on an unguarded `useEffect` to fetch directions — refiring every Google Directions call on each modal open, with an unbounded retry loop on `OVER_QUERY_LIMIT`, against an API billed per request.

## What changed

### Removed dead OpenLayers/guri code path
- Deleted `ItineraryMapOpenLayer.tsx`, `OpenLayerMap.jsx`, `ItinerarySynthesisContainer.js`.
- Removed the related Redux wiring: `address.actions.ts`, `address-guri.js` reducer, store registration, `action-types.js` entries, and the `api-endpoints.ts` guri endpoint.
- Removed the now-unused `ol` (OpenLayers) dependency from `package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml`.

### Migrated direction fetching to Tanstack Query
- Added `useItineraryDirections`, a `useQueries`-based hook that fetches Google Directions per unique place, replacing the old unguarded `useEffect`.
- Requests are now **cached** (`staleTime`/`gcTime`) instead of refiring on every modal open, and **retries are bounded** (`RETRY_LIMIT`) instead of looping indefinitely on `OVER_QUERY_LIMIT`.
- Renamed/simplified the map component to `ItineraryGoogleMap`, now driven by explicit `isLoading` / `currentDirection` props instead of the legacy container.

### Improved loading/error feedback
- `ItineraryGoogleMap` now distinguishes "still loading" from "no route available" instead of silently rendering an empty map.
- `ItinerarySynthesis` surfaces direction-fetch failures inline, with wording that accounts for partial failures (`useQueries` resolves each place independently, so some directions can fail while others still render).

## Removed

- :axe: `ol` (OpenLayers) package dependency.
- :axe: `ItineraryMapOpenLayer.tsx`, `OpenLayerMap.jsx`, `ItinerarySynthesisContainer.js`.
- :axe: Redux `guri` chain: `address.actions.ts`, `address-guri.js` reducer, store registration, related `action-types.js` and `api-endpoints.ts` entries.

## Migration path going forward

The `guri` backend integration was fully removed rather than preserved as-is: per the ticket, it "needs a complete rework/upgrade" if the backend-driven itinerary should ever be reintroduced — it should not be resurrected from this dead code
commits: refactor(ItinerarySynthesis): [IPERIA-8730] remove dead OpenLayers/guri code path and migrate direction fetching to Tanstack Query

+---
+2022/09/28
+
+---
+
+## Project folder structure
+
+### Context
+
+Over time, the number of classes into folders increase with new functionalities.
+Finding the class for a specific feature can be tricky.
+
+### Considered Options
+
+* Folder by feature structure.
+* 1 module per feature.
+
+### Decision
+
+Chosen option: Folder by feature structure.
+
+### Consequences
+
+* With this structure, we need to maintain the compiler pass to help Drupal discover plugins, entities etc...
+
+### Positive Consequences
+
+* Easier to find classes linked to a specific feature.
+* Class names can be reduced thanks to namespace (Calculator\BirthCounterAverageCalculator => BirthCounter\Calculator\AverageCalculator).
+* Increase SRP (Avoid to have 1 hook handler that serves multiple purposes).

@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+---
+2022/09/28
+
+---
+
+## Site type
+
+### Context
+
+The project contains more than one site type:
+* Corporate
+* Institution
+* International
+
+Some features don't need to be available on all types of site. Therefore, we need to check the site type in multiple places in the code.
+What is the best solution to avoid repeating the site type check everywhere?
+
+### Considered Options
+
+* Constants.
+* Enums.
+
+### Decision
+
+Chosen option: Enums.
+
+### Positive Consequences
+
+Avoid to spray site types logic everywhere.
+Centralize logic in Enums. Check is easier.
+Enums are a finished list: it throws exception if case does not match, then it forces us to consider each case.

-/**
- * Transform the result of a process to a compliant entity reference field.
- *
- * For the moment we stay KISS, no config.
- * The value should be an array looking like:
- *
- * @code
- * [
- *    'the target id as wanted by an EntityReferenceRevisions::setValue()',
- *    'the target revision id as wanted by an EntityReferenceRevisions::setValue()',
- * ]
- * @endcode
- *
- * The returned value as to be compliant
- * with EntityReferenceRevisions::setValue(). Hence the array of array.
- *
- * @MigrateProcessPlugin(
- *   id = "transform_to_compliant_entity_reference_field"
- * )
- *
- * @package Drupal\rgds_d7_migration\Plugin\migrate\process
- */
-final class TransformToCompliantEntityReferenceField extends ProcessPluginBase {
-
-  /**
-   * {@inheritdoc}
-   *
-   * phpcs:disable SlevomatCodingStandard.Functions.UnusedParameter
-   */
-  public function transform($value, MigrateExecutableInterface $migrate_executable, Row $row, $destination_property) {
-    $targetId = $value[0] ?? NULL;
-    $targetRevisionId = $value[1] ?? NULL;
-
-    if (empty($targetId) || empty($targetRevisionId)) {
-      return [];
-    }
-
-    return [
-      [
-        'target_id' => $targetId,
-        'target_revision_id' => $targetRevisionId,
-      ],
-    ];
-  }
-
-}

+<?php
+
+declare(strict_types=1);
+
+namespace src\Unit\Emergency\Model;
+
+use App\Tests\Unit\UnitTestCase;
+use Drupal\rgds_core\Emergency\Model\AverageTimes;
+
+final class AverageTimesTest extends UnitTestCase {
+
+  /**
+   * Average times validation rules.
+   *
+   * @dataProvider averageTimesCasesProvider
+   */
+  public function testAverageTimesValidation($expected, $values) {
+    $averageTimes = new AverageTimes(
+      $values['timestamp'],
+      $values['averageWaitingTime'],
+      $values['averageWaitingPatients'],
+      $values['averageTreatedPatients'],
+      $values['averageTraumatologyTime'],
+      $values['averageMedicineTime'],
+    );
+
+    self::assertSame($expected, $averageTimes->isValid());
+  }
+
+  public function averageTimesCasesProvider(): \Generator {
+    $timestamp = \time();
+    yield 'valid when positive numbers' => [
+      'expected' => TRUE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => 512,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 498,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 345,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 120,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 421,
+      ],
+    ];
+    yield 'valid when at least one positive numbers' => [
+      'expected' => TRUE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => 512,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 0,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 0,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 0,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 0,
+      ],
+    ];
+    yield 'valid when one zero numbers' => [
+      'expected' => TRUE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => 512,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 150,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 10,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 800,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 0,
+      ],
+    ];
+    yield 'invalid when empty' => [
+      'expected' => FALSE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => 0,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 0,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 0,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 0,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 0,
+      ],
+    ];
+    yield 'invalid when has only negative value' => [
+      'expected' => FALSE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => -15,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => -200,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => -900,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => -87,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => -1,
+      ],
+    ];
+    yield 'invalid when positive numbers and one negative value' =>
+    [
+      'expected' => FALSE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => -15,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 157,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 851,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 789,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 45,
+      ],
+    ];
+    yield 'invalid when zero numbers and one negative value' => [
+      'expected' => FALSE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => $timestamp,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => -15,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 0,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 0,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 0,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 0,
+      ],
+    ];
+
+    yield 'invalid when timestamp error and positive numbers' => [
+      'expected' => FALSE,
+      'values' => [
+        'timestamp' => 0,
+        'averageWaitingTime' => 1,
+        'averageWaitingPatients' => 1,
+        'averageTreatedPatients' => 1,
+        'averageTraumatologyTime' => 1,
+        'averageMedicineTime' => 1,
+      ],
+    ];
+  }
+
+}

title: [RGDSD8-1072] feat(seo): set seo recommendations on pagers
description:
## Summary

Closes RGDSD8-1072

### Details

In the pager, pager items' href just change the value of query parameters (page), to navigates over the different pages.

But SEO recommends not to have different URLs for the same resource. Here, `/actualites` = `/actualites?page=0` 

Then, the goal is to set first page to `/actualites` when possible.

### Note

On news list page, there is a search engine, that adds search key as a query parameter: `/actualites?key=test`

First page href must be `/actualites?key=test`  instead of `?key=test&page=0` in the pager.
commits: feat(seo): set seo recommendations on pagers

title: [RGDSD8-1099] fix(monolog_handler): fix default handler log permission with group write permission
description:
| Q | A |
|---|---|
| Tickets | [RGDSD8-1099](https://jira.ekino.com/browse/RGDSD8-1099) |
| Bug fix? | yes |
| New feature? | no |
| Deprecations? | no |

After the update from PHP 8.1 to PHP 8.3 we face a permission error when request generate a log througth PHP/Drupal : Logs file permissions are 0644 (file is generated in `app/logs/default` directory).

We need 0664 permission mode because cron job are triggered with a different user (ramsadmin), attach to www-data group, and write to this same file.

Reason why this behavior appear is unknown...
commits: fix(monolog_handler): fix default handler log permission with group write permission

@@ -8,11 +8,23 @@ parameters:
   monolog.rotation.nb_files.to_keep: 10
   monolog.default.handler.log_level: 100
   monolog.php.handler.log_level: 100
+  monolog.handler.bubble: true
+  monolog.handler.file_permission: 436 # Decimal for 0664 needed with php chmod.
 
 services:
   monolog.handler.default_handler:
     class: Monolog\Handler\RotatingFileHandler
-    arguments: ['%monolog.default.handler.storage_path%', '%monolog.rotation.nb_files.to_keep%', '%monolog.default.handler.log_level%']
+    arguments:
+      - '%monolog.default.handler.storage_path%'
+      - '%monolog.rotation.nb_files.to_keep%'
+      - '%monolog.default.handler.log_level%'
+      - '%monolog.handler.bubble%'
+      - '%monolog.handler.file_permission%'
   monolog.handler.php_handler:
     class: Monolog\Handler\RotatingFileHandler
-    arguments: ['%monolog.php.handler.storage_path%', '%monolog.rotation.nb_files.to_keep%', '%monolog.php.handler.log_level%']

+      - '%monolog.php.handler.log_level%'
+      - '%monolog.handler.bubble%'
+      - '%monolog.handler.file_permission%'

title: [RGDSD8-1056] feat(emergency) send an email with faillure or warnings report when import waiting times
description:
| Q | A |
|---|---|
| Tickets | RGDSD8-1056 |
| Bug fix? | no |
| New feature? | yes |
| Deprecations? | no |

Send an email with report on failure or warnings when flag is present in emergency waiting time import command.

E-mail recipient is based on env variable. It must be add in `.env` on server before deployed :

```ini
### Emergency Times Report emails. recipients are comma separate.
RGDS_EMERGENCY_SYNCHRO_REPORT_RECIPIENT="dev@test.it, change@emails.now"
```

title: [RGDSD8-1103] fix(emergency-import): import request content only when has CSV mime type
description:
| Q | A |
|---|---|
| Tickets | RGDSD8-1103 |
| Bug fix? | yes |
| New feature? | no |
| Deprecations? | no |

It has happened that Resurgence WS servers respond with `200 OK` while body content is html text describing an error.\
Checking declared content type will limit attempts to import non-CSV contents.

Content may have following valid mime types:

- text/csv
- text/plain
- application/octet-stream

title: [RGDSD8-1118] fix(drupal_settings): trusted host pattern is now extracted from an environment variable
description:
| Q | A |
|---|---|
| Tickets | RGDSD8-1118 |
| Bug fix? | no |
| New feature? | yes |
| Deprecations? | no |

Usage of environment variable for `trusted_host_patterns` setting, in order to avoid a deployment for each site creation with a not expected domain from trusted host regex.

It's mandatory to add in `shared/.env` file this line :

```
TRUSTED_HOST_PATTERNS='^(.*)\.rgds\.localdev$ ^(dev|((fix\.)?val)|www)\.ramsaysante\.eu$ ^(www|[a-z0-9_-]{4,60})\.((dev|(fix\.)?val)\.)?ramsaysante\.fr$ ^(dev\.|((fix\.)?val\.)|www\.)?institutepaulelille\.fr$'
```

> NB `institutepaulelille.fr` was added to regex. It is a new domain for an institution site.
commits: fix(drupal_settings): trusted host pattern is now extracted from an environment variable

 DRUPAL_CACHE_PAGE_MAX_AGE=31536000
 DRUPAL_FILE_PRIVATE_PATH=/app/var/files/private

+import {
+  Bold,
+  ClassicEditor,
+  Essentials,
+  Heading,
+  Italic,
+  FileRepository,
+  Image,
+  ImageUpload,
+  List,
+  Paragraph,
+} from 'ckeditor5';
+
+import 'ckeditor5/ckeditor5.css';
+
+import { Cropper } from './cropper/src/cropper';
+import { LocalUploadAdapter } from './local-upload-adapter/local-upload-adapter';
+
+function MyCustomUploadAdapterPlugin(editor) {
+  editor.plugins.get('FileRepository').createUploadAdapter = (loader) => {
+    return new LocalUploadAdapter(loader);
+  };
+}
+
+ClassicEditor.create(document.querySelector('#editor') as HTMLElement, {
+  plugins: [
+    Essentials,
+    FileRepository,
+    MyCustomUploadAdapterPlugin,
+    Image,
+    ImageUpload,
+    Bold,
+    Italic,
+    Heading,
+    List,
+    Paragraph,
+    Cropper,
+  ],
+  toolbar: [
+    'heading',
+    '|',
+    'bold',
+    'italic',
+    'numberedList',
+    'bulletedList',
+    'insertImage',
+    'cropper',
+  ],
+  licenseKey: 'GPL',
+})
+  .then((editor) => {
+    console.debug('Editor was initialized', editor);
+  })
+  .catch((error) => {
+    console.error(error.stack);
+  });

+# ckeditor5_cropper
+Cropper / Crop images in CKEditor5 editor.
+
+A Drupal way of cropping images in CKEditor5, based on cropperJs library.
+
+## To make changes
+```npm install```
+```npm run build```

+services:
+  ## Cropper
+  ckeditor5_cropper.image_cropper:
+    class: Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Cropper\ImageCropper
+    arguments:
+      - '@image.factory'
+      - '@file_system'
+      - '@ckeditor5_cropper.image_resolver_chain'
+  Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Cropper\ImageCropperInterface: '@ckeditor5_cropper.image_cropper'
+
+  ## Image Resolvers Chain
+  ckeditor5_cropper.image_resolver_chain:
+     class: Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Resolver\ImageResolverChain
+     calls:
+       - [addResolver, ['@ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.base64_image']]
+       - [addResolver, ['@ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.external_image']]
+       - [addResolver, ['@ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.same_domain_image']]
+       - [addResolver, ['@ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.local_image']]
+
+  ## Image Resolvers
+  ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.base64_image:
+    class: Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Resolver\Base64ImageResolver
+    arguments:
+      - '@file_system'
+
+  ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.external_image:
+    class: Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Resolver\ExternalImageResolver
+    arguments:
+      - '@http_client_factory'
+      - '@file_system'
+      - '@request_stack'
+
+  ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.same_domain_image:
+    class: Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Resolver\SameDomainImageResolver
+    arguments:
+      - '@file_system'
+      - '@file_url_generator'
+      - '@request_stack'
+
+  ckeditor5_cropper.resolver.local_image:
+    class: Drupal\ckeditor5_cropper\Resolver\LocalImageResolver
+    arguments:
+      - '@file_system'
+      - '@stream_wrapper_manager'

+import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
+import replace from '@rollup/plugin-replace';
+
+export default defineConfig(({ mode }) => {
+  const isProduction = mode === 'production';
+
+  // TODO: add a esm production build for comsumption outside of Drupal
+
+  return {
+    build: {
+      outDir: 'dist',
+      emptyOutDir: false,
+      minify: false,
+      lib: isProduction
+        ? {
+            entry: './js/ckeditor5_plugins/cropper/src/index.ts',
+            name: 'CKEditor5.cropper',
+            fileName: 'index.js',
+            formats: ['umd'],
+          }
+        : undefined,
+      rollupOptions: {
+        // Inside Drupal, CKEditor5 will already be loaded by other contrib plugins
+        // so we don't want to bundle it with our plugin, and instead
+        // we will use the global variable `CKEditor5` to access it
+        external: isProduction ? ['ckeditor5'] : undefined,
+        output: {
+          entryFileNames: 'index.js',
+          assetFileNames: 'index.css',
+          manualChunks: undefined,
+          format: isProduction ? 'umd' : undefined,
+          exports: isProduction ? 'default' : 'auto',
+          globals: isProduction ? { ckeditor5: 'CKEditor5' } : undefined,
+        },
+        plugins: [
+          // As we use the global `CKEditor5` variable in the UMD (Drupal targeted) build,
+          // we need to replace the imports with their location in the CKEditor5 global object.
+          // As the structure of this global object is not the same as the module imports,
+          // we need to replace the imports with the hard-coded paths...
+          isProduction &&
+            replace({
+              preventAssignment: true,
+              values: {
+                // core
+                'ckeditor5.Plugin': 'ckeditor5.core.Plugin',
+                'ckeditor5.Editor': 'ckeditor5.core.Editor',
+
+                // ui
+                'ckeditor5.View': 'ckeditor5.ui.View',
+                'ckeditor5.Dialog': 'ckeditor5.ui.Dialog',
+                'ckeditor5.ButtonView': 'ckeditor5.ui.ButtonView',
+
+                // image
+                'ckeditor5.ImageBlock': 'ckeditor5.image.ImageBlock',
+              },
+            }),
+        ],
+      },
+    },
+  };
+});

title: [RGDSD8-1125] chore(deps): update drupal from 10.6.2 to 11.2
description:
Update Drupal Core 10.6.2 to 11.2.11

Update dependencies to major version for 
- drupal/seven from v1.0 to 2.0beta
- brianium/paratest from 6.3 to 7.4
- phpunit/phpunit from 9.6 to 10.5

Patch adaptations :
- Drupal Core issue 2730351 CSRF check always fails for users without a session"
- Drupal Core custom patch: Move permission "view any unpublished content" from Content Moderation to Node
- Drupal Core custom patch: Remove useless Mink dependency.

Other: 
- replace Select2 with choices.js where form element is broken.

Refactoring for compatibility purpose and code quality fixes.
commits: fix(deprecation): category field type declaration for custom field item is no more translatable
chore(config): diff after updb from branch master installation to v11.2.11
fix(deps): composer semver to allow update for drupal scaffold package
refactor(choices): replace broken select2 element with a custom select with text filter element based on choices.js
refactor(choices): create custom form element and lib based on choices.js to replace select2 form element
fix(tests): workshop controller test use removed class in drupal 11
chore(security): update phpunit 10.5.60 to 10.5.63
chore(security): update drupal/core from 11.2.8 to 11.2.11
chore(quality): update phpstan baseline after rebase from develop
fix(d11): synchronize settings.php and services.yml with drupal 11 default
fix(workshop-slot-create): date range end value admin form js handling is broken and lets appear hidden field for date range end value
Revert "fix(e2e): add missing value for tested workshop form"
fix(e2e): add missing value for tested workshop form
chore(d11): remove reference to deprecated setting yaml_parser_class
chore(d11): remove reference to deprecated setting allow_authorize_operations
chore(D11): session.sid_length and session.sid_bits_per_character config have more secure symfony default values
chore(quality): update phpstan baseline and phpstan.neon.dist
chore(d11): appliy memory cache slot limit for LRU in memory backend strategy
chore(d11): Settings 'state_cache' is removed and permanently turned on
chore(deps): remove useless drupal ckeditor5_show_blocks module
fix(d11): quick node clone set wrong namespace for nodeform class
chore(quality): code quality fixes
chore(d11): replace drupal container_aware_event_dispatcher with symfony event_dispatcher
chore(deps): update micro-site to v3.0.0-alpha2 with no theme_suggest_page hook template override
chore(d11): remove deprecated module_implement_alter hook
fix(tests): add teardown to prevent exception when tests clear the request stack
fix(tests): add teardown to prevent exception when tests clear the request stack
fix(tests): use factory method to instanciate request in tests
fix(tests): enforce site directory creation for kernel file system tests
fix(tests) remove final keyword on extended class in tests
fix(tests): phpunit 10 remove support for withconsecutive method in mocks
chore(tests): phpunit configuration migration
fix(tests): tests execution with paratest
chore(d11): convert unsupported PDO::FETCH_FUNC
fix(compatibility): NodeForm class namespace has changed
chore(update): export configuration with drupal 11.2.3
chore(update): modules & patches bump
chore(update): scaffolded files update

title: [RGDSD8-1167] fix(theme): restore seven theme from claro theme
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1167
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no

For now theme update is not needed. ~~This WILL change with Drupal 11 update: Seven theme is no more in core but becomes a contributed theme.~~ Fake news 

Seven is already a contrib module since Drupal 10.
See change record from 2022: https://www.drupal.org/node/3304670

@see revision commit bf0a4d5709968287d8fd03595a63cc09885da744 for claro theme installation

## Caution: 
In the workshop form, date range slots use a custom date input with a custom JS script. This script uses a specific class selector to find date range field wrapper. This class may changes with some themes like claro.

@see: 
`app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/src/Plugin/Field/FieldWidget/HoursDateRangeWidget.php` that has js script `app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/js/rgds_core.hours_daterange_widget.js` dependency.
commits: fix(theme): restore seven theme from claro theme

title: [RGDSD8-1186] add predefined options and autocomplete-like lib integration
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1186
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | yes
| Deprecations? | no

To provide an autocomplete-like behaviour with an institution list we decide with the Christophe to use a simple predefined option list and use "choices" library.

Choices was preferred over Select2 because this later is no more maintenained and not compatible with JQuery 4 used in Drupal 11.

We try to be coherent with RGDS Style :
![Capture_d_écran_2026-03-13_à_09.31.21](/uploads/43203e1147d2f83ae56c7621bb5de32f/Capture_d_écran_2026-03-13_à_09.31.21.png){width=900 height=443}


to approach SPA select design : 
![image](/uploads/eba9aee2266916283733f25732d1caee/image.png){width=900 height=390}
commits: feat(choices-js): usable display limit for choices results and improve choice graphic integration with rgds theme

title: [RGDSD8-1187] feat(site-list): contact page site institution list with autocomplete filter and corporate option
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1187
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | yes
| Deprecations? | no

| Video |
| ------ |
| ![contact-list-demo](/uploads/18d33e30266fc363dfdb970502325f52/contact-list-demo.mp4){width=900 height=507} |

We expect than `choices.js` is available to be default auto-complete select style with webform and we force its use with contact page institution list select element.

This opinionated presupposed break JS handling, so we need to adapt JS to maintain global behaviour (redirect to contact page for selected site).

test(institution-list): update test with new behavior
feat(institution-list): force choices as main rendering
fix(institution-list): sort algo

title: [RGDSD8-1194] update PHPUnit 10.5 to PHPUnit 11.5 for D11 update
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1194
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | yes

- Resolve phpunit 10 deprecations whose are not more supported in phpunit 11
  - data providers must be static
  - named parameters in data providers must coincide with method arguments
  - annotation to attribute
- bump phpunit from 10.5 to 11.5
- resolve a couple of breaking changes with test suite and boostrap generation
commits: chore(phpunit): remove remaining dataprovider and deprecation
chore(phpunit): set env SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER from composer.json post-script call into the script itself
chore(tests): split branching data provider into dedicated test methods
chore(tests): use named data-set keys for phpunit 11 named arguments
chore(phpstan): remove unecessary ignored error after rebase
chore(deps): update phpunit from v10.5 to 11.5
chore(tests): once and any methods are no more static in phpunit 11 testcase class
chore(tests): remove bad named parameters in dataprovider not allowed in phpunit 11
chore(tests): dataprovider annotations is deprecated, migrate to attributes
chore(tests): dataprovider to static function for phpunit 11 compatibility
chore(deps): remove useless drupal ckeditor5_show_blocks module
chore(update): modules & patches bump
chore(quality): update phpstan baseline after rebase from develop
Revert "fix(e2e): add missing value for tested workshop form"
fix(e2e): add missing value for tested workshop form
chore(quality): update phpstan baseline and phpstan.neon.dist
chore(quality): code quality fixes
chore(update): modules & patches bump
