title: [NOJIRA] ci: reduce noise and false positives from sonar analysis
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | NOJIRA
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no

Restrict analysis to meaningful code only to reduce noise and false positives.

- Exclude *.theme and *.tokens.inc from coverage (hook glue code, untestable in isolation)
- Exclude *.theme, *.tokens.inc and Form/** from CPD (framework-forced structural repetition, not knowledge duplication)
- Exclude *.js from coverage (not covered by PHPUnit)
- Exclude rgds_theme from analysis entirely (mainly front team territory, no actionable issues at this stage, main team is on vacation, it creates noises for the moment)
- Exclude app/sites/**, app/autoload.php, app/index.php, app/web.config from analysis (Drupal bootstrap boilerplate and entry points, no business logic)

cc @pascal.marzo
commits: ci: reduce noise and false positives from sonar analysis

files.diff:
@@ -219,9 +219,9 @@ sonar:
   stage: !reference [nightly:phpunit:coverage, stage]
   needs: ["nightly:phpunit:coverage"]
   variables:
-    SONAR_COVERAGE_EXCLUSIONS: "**/*.module,**/*.install,**/*.post_update.php,**/Entity/**,**/Plugin/**"
-    SONAR_CPD_EXCLUSIONS: "**/*.module,**/*.install,**/*.post_update.php,**/Entity/**,**/Plugin/**,**/config/**,**/*.info.yml,**/*.libraries.yml,**/*.links.action.yml,**/*.links.menu.yml,**/*.links.task.yml,**/*.permissions.yml"
-    SONAR_EXCLUSIONS: "app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/tests/**/*"
+    SONAR_COVERAGE_EXCLUSIONS: "**/*.theme,**/*.module,**/*.install,**/*.post_update.php,**/*.tokens.inc,**/Entity/**,**/Plugin/**,**/*.js"
+    SONAR_CPD_EXCLUSIONS: "**/*.theme,**/*.module,**/*.install,**/*.post_update.php,**/*.tokens.inc,**/Entity/**,**/Plugin/**,**/Form/**,**/config/**,**/*.info.yml,**/*.libraries.yml,**/*.links.action.yml,**/*.links.menu.yml,**/*.links.task.yml,**/*.permissions.yml"
+    SONAR_EXCLUSIONS: "app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/**/*,app/sites/**/*,app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/tests/**/*,app/autoload.php,app/index.php,app/web.config"
     SONAR_PHP_COVERAGE_REPORT_PATHS: "build/phpunit/coverage/clover.xml"
     SONAR_PHP_TESTS: "build/phpunit/logging/junit.xml"
     SONAR_SOURCES: "app"

title: [RGDSD8-1204] feat(workshop): allow contributor to define extra inputs on the workshop registration.
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1204
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | yes
| Deprecations? | no

- [X] contributor may define extra inputs per workshop.
- [X] extra inputs are saved when a user register to a workshop slot. Extra inputs definitions and values are stored directly on the workshop registration to save as a snapshop (contributor may delete an extra inputs from a workshop with regsitration)
- [X] list workshop registration display a column "extra inputs": for the moment stay simple to see if it passed or not for the client to avoid too much complexity.
- [X] from this list, the exports have the extra inputs. Each extra input have its own column
- [X] drush commands export used in cronjobs also support extra inputs.
- [X] mails send to the registered user and the manager of the workshop take into account the extra inputs. The id of the extra input is used as the replacement token, i.e. `[id]`, like the rest of the tokens.
- [x] frontend part to handle the extra inputs, @maxime.dubourg 

## Doc for frontend team @maxime.dubourg 

The extra inputs are displayed in the form in the twig template `app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/templates/node/node--workshop--teaser.html.twig`

To submit the form, you need to add to the current POST to `/save-workshop-registration` the form data for these extra inputs.
If we documented it using OpenApi schema, the request body would look like this:

```yaml
    WorkshopRegistrationRequest:
      type: object
      required:
        - workshop_id
        - workshop_slot_id
        - lastname
        - firstname
        - phone
        - email
      properties:
        workshop_id:
          type: integer
          description: Node ID of the workshop.
          example: 42
        workshop_slot_id:
          type: integer
          description: Paragraph ID of the selected workshop slot.
          example: 7
        lastname:
          type: string
          description: Registrant last name.
          example: Dupont
        firstname:
          type: string
          description: Registrant first name.
          example: Marie
        phone:
          type: string
          description: Registrant phone number.
          example: "0610203040"
        email:
          type: string
          format: email
          description: Registrant email address.
          example: marie.dupont@example.com
        delivery_date:
          type: string
          description: >
            Expected childbirth delivery date in dd/mm/yyyy format.
            Required for maternity workshops (field_is_generic_workshop is false).
            Must not be provided for generic workshops.
          example: "25/12/2025"
        can_have_companion:
          type: string
          enum: ["1"]
          description: >
            Must be present (with value "1") when the workshop allows a companion
            (field_can_have_companion is true), and must be absent otherwise.
          example: "1"
        extra_inputs:
          type: object
          description: >
            Answers to the workshop's extra input fields, keyed by the extra
            input identifier defined in the definition (see workshop's field_extra_inputs). Required extra
            inputs must be non-empty strings. Optional extra inputs may be
            omitted. Values must be strings (not arrays or numbers).
          additionalProperties:
            type: string
          example:
            diet: "vegetarian"
```
commits: feat(workshop): validate and submit extra inputs during workshop registration
feat(workshop): allow contributor to define extra inputs on the workshop registration

+<?php
+
+declare(strict_types=1);
+
+namespace Drupal\Tests\rgds_core\Unit\Workshop\Entity\WorkshopRegistration;
+
+use Drupal\Tests\UnitTestCase;
+use Drupal\rgds_core\Workshop\Entity\Workshop\ExtraInput\Type;
+use Drupal\rgds_core\Workshop\Entity\WorkshopRegistration\ExtraInput;
+use Drupal\rgds_core\Workshop\Exception\InvalidExtraInputException;
+
+final class ExtraInputTest extends UnitTestCase {
+
+  public function testItShouldCreateFromValidArray(): void {
+    $extraInput = ExtraInput::fromArray([
+      'id' => 'name',
+      'label' => 'Full name',
+      'type' => 'text',
+      'required' => TRUE,
+      'value' => 'Alice',
+    ]);
+
+    self::assertSame('name', $extraInput->id);
+    self::assertSame('Full name', $extraInput->label);
+    self::assertSame(Type::Text, $extraInput->type);
+    self::assertTrue($extraInput->isRequired);
+    self::assertSame('Alice', $extraInput->value);
+  }
+
+  public function testItShouldCreateFromValidArrayWithNullValue(): void {
+    $extraInput = ExtraInput::fromArray([
+      'id' => 'comment',
+      'label' => 'Comment',
+      'type' => 'text',
+      'required' => FALSE,
+      'value' => NULL,
+    ]);
+
+    self::assertNull($extraInput->value);
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Asserts that fromArray throws for invalid entries.
+   *
+   * @param mixed $entry
+   *   The raw entry to parse.
+   * @param string $exceptionMessage
+   *   The expected exception message (partial match).
+   *
+   * @dataProvider provideInvalidFromArrayCases
+   */
+  public function testItShouldThrowWhenFromArrayReceivesInvalidEntry(
+    mixed $entry,
+    string $exceptionMessage,
+  ): void {
+    $this->expectException(InvalidExtraInputException::class);
+    $this->expectExceptionMessage($exceptionMessage);
+
+    ExtraInput::fromArray($entry);
+  }
+
+  public function testItShouldThrowWhenTypeIsUnknown(): void {
+    $this->expectException(\ValueError::class);
+    $this->expectExceptionMessage('"unknown" is not a valid backing value for enum');
+
+    ExtraInput::fromArray([
+      'id' => 'x',
+      'label' => 'L',
+      'type' => 'unknown',
+      'required' => TRUE,
+      'value' => NULL,
+    ]);
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Provides invalid entries for fromArray error cases.
+   *
+   * @return array<string, array{mixed, string}>
+   *   Tuples of [entry, exceptionMessage].
+   */
+  public static function provideInvalidFromArrayCases(): array {
+    return [
+      'missing id key' => [
+        ['label' => 'L', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input id must be a non empty string.',
+      ],
+      'empty id' => [
+        ['id' => '', 'label' => 'L', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input id must be a non empty string.',
+      ],
+      'non-string id' => [
+        ['id' => 123, 'label' => 'L', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input id must be a non empty string.',
+      ],
+      'missing label key' => [
+        ['id' => 'x', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input label must be a non empty string.',
+      ],
+      'empty label' => [
+        ['id' => 'x', 'label' => '', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input label must be a non empty string.',
+      ],
+      'missing type key' => [
+        ['id' => 'x', 'label' => 'L', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input type must be a non empty string.',
+      ],
+      'missing required key' => [
+        ['id' => 'x', 'label' => 'L', 'type' => 'text', 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input required must be a boolean.',
+      ],
+      'non-bool required' => [
+        ['id' => 'x', 'label' => 'L', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => 'yes', 'value' => NULL],
+        'Extra input required must be a boolean.',
+      ],
+      'non-string value' => [
+        ['id' => 'x', 'label' => 'L', 'type' => 'text', 'required' => TRUE, 'value' => 123],
+        'Extra input value must be a string or null.',
+      ],
+    ];
+  }
+
+}

files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+# CLAUDE.md
+
+This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
+
+## Project Overview
+
+Drupal 11 multisite project ("website factory") for RGDS, built with a custom install profile (`rgds`). Hosted on Platform.sh, developed with Docker locally, CI/CD via GitLab.
+
+## Development Environment
+
+```bash
+make install          # First-time setup (Docker required)
+make run              # Start all services (foreground)
+make upgrade          # After git pull: yarn + composer + drupal upgrade
+make docker-shell-php # Shell into the PHP container
+make drush cmd='...'  # Run drush commands
+```
+
+All PHP commands (composer, drush, phpunit, phpcs, etc.) run inside the Docker PHP container. Use `make docker-shell-php` to get a shell, or prefix with `docker compose exec --user www-data php`.
+
+## Quality & Testing
+
+Run inside the PHP container:
+
+```bash
+# Code analysis
+./bin/phpcs                                           # PHP_CodeSniffer (EkinoDrupal + Slevomat rules)
+./bin/phpmd ./app/modules/custom,./app/profiles/rgds/modules ansi phpmd.xml.dist
+./bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M             # PHPStan level: max. NEVER RUN PHPSTAN ON A SUBSET OF FILES.
+
+# Tests
+./bin/phpunit --testsuite rgds_unit                   # Unit tests only
+./bin/phpunit --testsuite rgds_kernel_1               # Kernel tests (suites 1-4 + rgds_others)
+./bin/phpunit --filter=SomeTestClass                  # Single test class
+./bin/phpunit --filter=testMethodName                 # Single test method
+
+# Twig linting (runs via Node Docker container)
+make twig-lint-check
+make twig-lint-fix
+```
+
+Test suites are split into `rgds_unit`, `rgds_kernel_1` through `rgds_kernel_4`, `rgds_kernel_custom_module`, and `rgds_others` for CI parallelization. Tests use SQLite in-memory and the `DG\BypassFinals` PHPUnit extension.
+
+## Architecture
+
+### Directory Layout
+
+- `app/` is the Drupal web root
+- `app/profiles/rgds/` is the custom install profile
+- `app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/` is the single custom module (all custom functionality lives here)
+- `app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/` is the custom theme (extends Stable9, uses Tailwind CSS)
+- `app/modules/custom/` has a legacy migration module (`rgds_d7_migration`)
+- `config/sync/` holds all exported Drupal configuration
+- `tests/` holds project-level test utilities (autoloaded as `App\Tests\` namespace)
+
+### Hook Handler Pattern
+
+Hooks are NOT implemented as procedural functions in the `.module` file. Instead, `rgds_core.module` delegates to dedicated **HookHandler** classes resolved via `Drupal::service('class_resolver')`.
+
+Hook handlers live in `src/HookHandler/` organized by hook type:
+- `HookHandler/Entity/` (access, bundle info, field info, form, view, pre-delete)
+- `HookHandler/Form/Node/` (node form alterations)
+- `HookHandler/Preprocess/Block/`, `HookHandler/Preprocess/Paragraph/` (template preprocessing)
+- `HookHandler/Mail/`, `HookHandler/Toolbar/`, `HookHandler/ThemeSuggestions/`, `HookHandler/PageAttachments/`
+
+Feature-specific hook handlers live within their feature directory (e.g., `Emergency/HookHandler/`, `Finance/HookHandler/`, `Workshop/HookHandler/`).
+
+### Feature Organization
+
+Custom code is organized by domain within `rgds_core/src/`:
+`AlertMessage`, `BirthsCounter`, `Breadcrumb`, `Cache`, `Commands`, `Config`, `ContactPage`, `Controller`, `Emergency`, `Entity`, `Enum`, `Finance`, `Finder`, `Form`, `Institution`, `InstitutionRating`, `InternationalSite`, `JobOffer`, `LegalNotice`, `Menu`, `Metatag`, `Model`, `Navigation`, `News`, `ParagraphLibrary`, `PathAlias`, `PaymentLink`, `Plugin`, `Prevention`, `Resolver`, `RgdsApiClient`, `RobotsTxt`, `ScheduledPublication`, `Search`, `SiteFactory`, `Sitemap`, `StoreLocator`, `Submission`, `Tokens`, `Twig`, `User`, `Workshop`
+
+### Workshop Subsystem
+
+The Workshop feature is the most complex, with its own `Controller/`, `Entity/`, `Form/`, `Plugin/`, `Batch/`, `Commands/`, `Export/`, `Finder/`, `Query/`, `HookHandler/`, and `Tests/` subdirectories.
+
+### Exception / Error handling
+
+When throwing an exception, either use the `\Drupal\rgds_core\Exception\NotSupportedException` for generic case or create a custom exception class in the relevant feature namespace (e.g., `Workshop\Exception\`).
+This allows for more specific catch blocks and better error handling.
+
+### Tests
+
+Do not use PHPUnit `#[Test]` attributes.
+Naming convention: `itShouldExpectedBehaviorWhenStateUnderTest`.
+
+If Drupal config changed, it is required to execute the script `./scripts/manage-tests-module.sh --create` inside PHP container to regenerate the `tests/modules/rgds_test_config` module with the updated config.
+We cannot expect Kernel tests using nex configs to pass if the test module is not regenerated after config changes.
+
+## Coding Standards (enforced by phpcs.xml.dist)
+
+- `declare(strict_types=1)` required in all PHP files
+- Yoda comparisons required (`'value' === $var`)
+- Early exit pattern enforced (no unnecessary else blocks)
+- Static closures when `$this` is not used
+- Fully qualified global functions and constants (`\array_map`, `\PHP_EOL`)
+- Alphabetically sorted `use` statements (case-sensitive)
+- Trailing commas in multiline arrays
+- Class constant visibility required
+- `===`/`!==` only (no `==`/`!=`)
+- Property type hints required (PHPDoc only, native disabled)
+- Prefer loop to successive `\array_map`, `\array_filter`..
+- EkinoDrupalCodingStandard as base ruleset
+
+## Git Conventions
+
+See [Contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).
+
+## Key Technical Details
+
+- PHP 8.3, Drupal 11.2.x
+- Database: PostgreSQL 16
+- Caching: Redis + Varnish
+- PHPStan at level `max` with drupal extension and baseline
+- Composer bin directory: `./bin` (so `./bin/phpunit`, `./bin/phpcs`, etc.)
+- The project uses `drupal-paranoia` (separate `app/` and `web/` directories)
+- Micro-suite integration: `micro_menu`, `micro_node`, `micro_site`, `micro_sso`, `micro_user` (multisite infrastructure)

+
+  public function testItShouldCreateFromValidArray(): void {

+

+    self::assertSame('Full name', $extraInput->label);
+    self::assertSame(Type::Text, $extraInput->type);

+    self::assertSame('Alice', $extraInput->value);

+
+  public function testItShouldCreateFromValidArrayWithNullValue(): void {
+    $extraInput = ExtraInput::fromArray([
+      'id' => 'comment',

+# CLAUDE.md
+
+This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
+
+## Project Overview
+
+Drupal 11 multisite project ("website factory") for RGDS, built with a custom install profile (`rgds`). Hosted on Platform.sh, developed with Docker locally, CI/CD via GitLab.
+
+## Development Environment
+
+```bash
+make install          # First-time setup (Docker required)
+make run              # Start all services (foreground)
+make upgrade          # After git pull: yarn + composer + drupal upgrade
+make docker-shell-php # Shell into the PHP container
+make drush cmd='...'  # Run drush commands
+```
+
+All PHP commands (composer, drush, phpunit, phpcs, etc.) run inside the Docker PHP container. Use `make docker-shell-php` to get a shell, or prefix with `docker compose exec --user www-data php`.
+
+## Quality & Testing
+
+Run inside the PHP container:
+
+```bash
+# Code analysis
+./bin/phpcs                                           # PHP_CodeSniffer (EkinoDrupal + Slevomat rules)
+./bin/phpmd ./app/modules/custom,./app/profiles/rgds/modules ansi phpmd.xml.dist
+./bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M             # PHPStan level: max. NEVER RUN PHPSTAN ON A SUBSET OF FILES.
+
+# Tests
+./bin/phpunit --testsuite rgds_unit                   # Unit tests only
+./bin/phpunit --testsuite rgds_kernel_1               # Kernel tests (suites 1-4 + rgds_others)
+./bin/phpunit --filter=SomeTestClass                  # Single test class
+./bin/phpunit --filter=testMethodName                 # Single test method
+
+# Twig linting (runs via Node Docker container)
+make twig-lint-check
+make twig-lint-fix
+```
+
+Test suites are split into `rgds_unit`, `rgds_kernel_1` through `rgds_kernel_4`, `rgds_kernel_custom_module`, and `rgds_others` for CI parallelization. Tests use SQLite in-memory and the `DG\BypassFinals` PHPUnit extension.
+
+## Architecture
+
+### Directory Layout
+
+- `app/` is the Drupal web root
+- `app/profiles/rgds/` is the custom install profile
+- `app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/` is the single custom module (all custom functionality lives here)
+- `app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/` is the custom theme (extends Stable9, uses Tailwind CSS)
+- `app/modules/custom/` has a legacy migration module (`rgds_d7_migration`)
+- `config/sync/` holds all exported Drupal configuration
+- `tests/` holds project-level test utilities (autoloaded as `App\Tests\` namespace)
+
+### Hook Handler Pattern
+
+Hooks are NOT implemented as procedural functions in the `.module` file. Instead, `rgds_core.module` delegates to dedicated **HookHandler** classes resolved via `Drupal::service('class_resolver')`.
+
+Hook handlers live in `src/HookHandler/` organized by hook type:
+- `HookHandler/Entity/` (access, bundle info, field info, form, view, pre-delete)
+- `HookHandler/Form/Node/` (node form alterations)
+- `HookHandler/Preprocess/Block/`, `HookHandler/Preprocess/Paragraph/` (template preprocessing)
+- `HookHandler/Mail/`, `HookHandler/Toolbar/`, `HookHandler/ThemeSuggestions/`, `HookHandler/PageAttachments/`
+
+Feature-specific hook handlers live within their feature directory (e.g., `Emergency/HookHandler/`, `Finance/HookHandler/`, `Workshop/HookHandler/`).
+
+### Feature Organization
+
+Custom code is organized by domain within `rgds_core/src/`:
+`AlertMessage`, `BirthsCounter`, `Breadcrumb`, `Cache`, `Commands`, `Config`, `ContactPage`, `Controller`, `Emergency`, `Entity`, `Enum`, `Finance`, `Finder`, `Form`, `Institution`, `InstitutionRating`, `InternationalSite`, `JobOffer`, `LegalNotice`, `Menu`, `Metatag`, `Model`, `Navigation`, `News`, `ParagraphLibrary`, `PathAlias`, `PaymentLink`, `Plugin`, `Prevention`, `Resolver`, `RgdsApiClient`, `RobotsTxt`, `ScheduledPublication`, `Search`, `SiteFactory`, `Sitemap`, `StoreLocator`, `Submission`, `Tokens`, `Twig`, `User`, `Workshop`
+
+### Workshop Subsystem
+
+The Workshop feature is the most complex, with its own `Controller/`, `Entity/`, `Form/`, `Plugin/`, `Batch/`, `Commands/`, `Export/`, `Finder/`, `Query/`, `HookHandler/`, and `Tests/` subdirectories.
+
+### Exception / Error handling
+
+When throwing an exception, either use the `\Drupal\rgds_core\Exception\NotSupportedException` for generic case or create a custom exception class in the relevant feature namespace (e.g., `Workshop\Exception\`).
+This allows for more specific catch blocks and better error handling.
+
+### Tests
+
+Do not use PHPUnit `#[Test]` attributes.
+Naming convention: `itShouldExpectedBehaviorWhenStateUnderTest`.
+
+If Drupal config changed, it is required to execute the script `./scripts/manage-tests-module.sh --create` inside PHP container to regenerate the `tests/modules/rgds_test_config` module with the updated config.
+We cannot expect Kernel tests using nex configs to pass if the test module is not regenerated after config changes.
+
+## Coding Standards (enforced by phpcs.xml.dist)
+
+- `declare(strict_types=1)` required in all PHP files
+- Yoda comparisons required (`'value' === $var`)
+- Early exit pattern enforced (no unnecessary else blocks)
+- Static closures when `$this` is not used
+- Fully qualified global functions and constants (`\array_map`, `\PHP_EOL`)
+- Alphabetically sorted `use` statements (case-sensitive)
+- Trailing commas in multiline arrays
+- Class constant visibility required
+- `===`/`!==` only (no `==`/`!=`)
+- Property type hints required (PHPDoc only, native disabled)
+- Prefer loop to successive `\array_map`, `\array_filter`..
+- EkinoDrupalCodingStandard as base ruleset
+
+## Git Conventions
+
+See [Contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).
+
+## Key Technical Details
+
+- PHP 8.3, Drupal 11.2.x
+- Database: PostgreSQL 16
+- Caching: Redis + Varnish
+- PHPStan at level `max` with drupal extension and baseline
+- Composer bin directory: `./bin` (so `./bin/phpunit`, `./bin/phpcs`, etc.)
+- The project uses `drupal-paranoia` (separate `app/` and `web/` directories)
+- Micro-suite integration: `micro_menu`, `micro_node`, `micro_site`, `micro_sso`, `micro_user` (multisite infrastructure)

files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+<?php
+
+declare(strict_types=1);
+
+namespace Drupal\rgds_core\Finance\Finder;
+
+use Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface;
+use Drupal\rgds_core\Finance\Controller\Api\WiztrustPostFinancePage\Langcode;
+
+final readonly class WiztrustCategoryTermFinder {
+
+  public function __construct(
+    private EntityTypeManagerInterface $entityTypeManager,
+  ) {}
+
+  /**
+   * Resolve category names to taxonomy term entities.
+   *
+   * @param non-empty-string[] $categoryNames
+   *   Category names to findByNameAccordingToLangcode.
+   * @param \Drupal\rgds_core\Finance\Controller\Api\WiztrustPostFinancePage\Langcode $langcode
+   *   The language code determining which vocabularies to search.
+   *
+   * @return \Drupal\taxonomy\TermInterface[]
+   *   Matched taxonomy terms. Non-matching names are silently ignored.
+   */
+  public function findByNamesAccordingToLangcode(array $categoryNames, Langcode $langcode): array {
+    $ids = $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage('taxonomy_term')->getQuery()
+      ->accessCheck(FALSE)
+      ->condition('name', $categoryNames, 'IN')
+      ->condition('vid', $langcode->vocabularies(), 'IN')
+      ->execute();
+
+    return $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage('taxonomy_term')->loadMultiple($ids);
+  }
+
+}

files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+<?php
+
+declare(strict_types=1);
+
+namespace Drupal\rgds_core\Finance\Finder;
+
+use Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface;
+use Drupal\rgds_core\Wiztrust\HttpClient\Item\Langcode;
+
+final readonly class WiztrustCategoryTermFinder {
+
+  public function __construct(
+    private EntityTypeManagerInterface $entityTypeManager,
+  ) {}
+
+  /**
+   * Resolve category names to taxonomy term entities.
+   *
+   * @param non-empty-string[] $categoryNames
+   *   Category names to findByNameAccordingToLangcode.
+   * @param \Drupal\rgds_core\Wiztrust\HttpClient\Item\Langcode $langcode
+   *   The language code determining which vocabularies to search.
+   *
+   * @return \Drupal\taxonomy\TermInterface[]
+   *   Matched taxonomy terms. Non-matching names are silently ignored.
+   */
+  public function findByNamesAccordingToLangcode(array $categoryNames, Langcode $langcode): array {
+    $ids = $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage('taxonomy_term')->getQuery()
+      ->accessCheck(FALSE)
+      ->condition('name', $categoryNames, 'IN')
+      ->condition('vid', $langcode->vocabularies(), 'IN')
+      ->execute();
+
+    return $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage('taxonomy_term')->loadMultiple($ids);
+  }

description:

| Tickets       | NOJIRA

| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no

enable `reportIgnoresWithoutComments`: see https://phpstan.org/user-guide/ignoring-errors#requiring-comments-for-%40phpstan-ignore

**Every ignored error should be to documented.**

As a consequence, replace the now-disallowed blanket `@phpstan-ignore-next-line`
with identifier-based, documented ignores:
- WorkshopRegistrationExportBatch: method.nonObject, argument.type on the
  field_date_range->start_date magic property resolved as mixed instead of
  DrupalDateTime;
- IsLegalNoticeAccessibleAccess: argument.type on the site entity known to be
  a SiteInterface (also extract the SiteType into a variable);
- SiteWebformListBuilder: method.notFound on the untyped
  WebformEntityListBuilder::database property;
- document the ignoreErrors entries in phpstan.neon.dist;
- add a "Handling PHPStan errors" section to CLAUDE.md.
commits: chore(phpstan): require every inline ignored error to be documented

 Test suites are split into `rgds_unit`, `rgds_kernel_1` through `rgds_kernel_4`, `rgds_kernel_custom_module`, and `rgds_others` for CI parallelization. Tests use SQLite in-memory and the `DG\BypassFinals` PHPUnit extension.
 
+### Handling PHPStan errors
+
+Every ignored error must be documented (`reportIgnoresWithoutComments: true`): explain if it is a false positive and why, or if it is real why it is not fixed, and what should be done (TODO).
+Ask yourself questions like: Is it a false positive? If yes why? If no why ignoring it? Is it a known issue? Should we contribute to something?
+
+- **False positive**: ignore it with a comment.
+- **Real error**: either fix it, or ignore it with a comment justifying why it is not fixed. If the same kind of error is already ignored in `phpstan.neon.dist`, add the new occurrence there too, to keep identical errors grouped together.
+
+Two ways to ignore, in order of preference:
+
+1. Inline, close to the code: `// @phpstan-ignore <identifier> (why it is ignored and what to do)`. For several errors on one line, give each identifier its own comment: `<id1> (reason), <id2> (reason)`. The parser is naive: do not put `,` or `()` inside a comment (write `getTimestamp` not `getTimestamp()`), otherwise the comment is not detected.
+2. Centralized in `phpstan.neon.dist` under `ignoreErrors`, with a preceding `#` comment. Use this when the same error repeats across files or is already grouped there.
+
+`phpstan-baseline.neon` is the legacy baseline: errors are unsorted and each entry is triage work. It must only shrink over time, by qualifying entries as false positives (move to a documented ignore) or by fixing them. Never regenerate it to hide new errors without asking the user its consent.
+
 ## Architecture
 
 ### Directory Layout

title: [RGDSD8-1208] fix(mapbox): repair Windows-1252 bytes inside store locator CSV file import
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1208
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no

Exports mix both encodings within a single file, so deciding on the whole
content turned every already-valid accent into mojibake as soon as one stray
byte was present. The decision is now taken sequence by sequence, which leaves
valid UTF-8 byte for byte untouched.

Byte order marks are honoured first since they state the encoding rather than
guess it, which also brings UTF-16 and UTF-32 support. The UTF-8 BOM was
already skipped by Symfony CsvEncoder but is now stripped upstream so the
parser stops depending on it, the serializer being meant to go away.
commits: fix(encoding): repair Windows-1252 bytes inside store locator CSV files

+    yield 'utf-8 without bom' => [$utf8];
+    yield 'utf-8 with bom' => ["\xEF\xBB\xBF" . $utf8];

+    yield 'utf-16le with bom' => ["\xFF\xFE" . (string) \mb_convert_encoding($utf8, 'UTF-16LE', 'UTF-8')];

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+---
+2026/09/03
+
+---
+
+## Tailwind preset delivered by the frontend CI
+
+### Context
+
+The Tailwind design system (tokens, base styles, `btn--*` components) is owned by the ui-kit of the
+[frontend monorepo](https://gitlab.ekino.com/rgds/rgds-website-factory-frontend). With Tailwind 3,
+this repository installed the whole monorepo as a git npm dependency (`#master`, with a deploy token
+written in clear in `package.json`), copied `index.css` and `tailwind.config.js` in a `postinstall`
+script, and relied on a relative `require('./tailwind-purge')` inside the copied config to inject its
+own Twig/JS sources and safelist.
+
+Tailwind 4 moves the configuration to CSS (`preset.css` = `theme.css` + `base.css` +
+`components.css`, without any `@source`) and drops the JS `safelist`: the copy/`require` trick no
+longer works, and the git dependency had to be frozen and its token removed anyway.
+
+### Considered Options
+
+* Keep the git npm dependency, pinned on a SHA, with credentials injected from the environment
+  (`.env`, CI variable) through a git `insteadOf` configuration.
+* Have the existing `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the frontend repository copy the four preset
+  files into `app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/`, next to the SPA bundles it
+  already delivers, and drop the npm dependency.
+
+### Decision
+
+Chosen option: the preset is copied by the `drupal-bundles:update` job.
+
+`tailwind.css` (repository root) imports `tailwindcss`, then the local copy of `preset.css`, and
+declares the sources to scan. The ex-safelist becomes `@source inline(...)` directives.
+
+### Positive Consequences
+
+No secret in the repository, no SHA to maintain, no clone of the monorepo on each `yarn` install.
+SPA bundles and preset always come from the same frontend commit, so the classes used by the bundles
+are always known by the preset that compiles them.
+
+### Negative Consequences
+
+The preset files are duplicated in this repository and must never be edited here: any change goes
+through the frontend monorepo and a run of the `drupal-bundles:update` job.

+/*
+ * Tailwind CSS 4 entry point of the rgds_theme theme (built with `yarn build:stylesheet`).
+ *
+ * The ui-kit preset (design tokens, base styles, shared components) lives in
+ * app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/. It is a copy pushed by the
+ * `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the rgds-website-factory-frontend repository, along with the
+ * SPA bundles: do not edit it here, change it in the frontend monorepo instead.
+ *
+ * `@source` paths are relative to this file.
+ *
+ * Utilities are deliberately emitted OUTSIDE of the `utilities` cascade layer (the expanded form of
+ * `@import 'tailwindcss'`, without `layer(utilities)`): Drupal core, contrib modules and the theme
+ * component stylesheets are not layered, and a layered utility always loses against them whatever
+ * the source order or specificity (e.g. core `.hidden` would beat `md:block`, a theme rule would
+ * beat `flex` or `bg-white`). Unlayered utilities keep the Tailwind 3 cascade (order + specificity).
+ */
+@layer theme, base, components, utilities;
+@import 'tailwindcss/theme.css' layer(theme);
+@import 'tailwindcss/preflight.css' layer(base);
+@import 'tailwindcss/utilities.css' source(none);
+@import './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/preset.css';
+
+/* ===== SOURCES ===== */
+
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/templates';
+/* Includes the minified SPA bundles, whose classes must exist in this stylesheet. */
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/js';
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/templates';
+
+/* ===== DYNAMIC CLASSES (ex safelist) ===== */
+
+/* node--emergencies-page--full.html.twig: grid-cols-{{ node.field_chapters.value|length }} */
+@source inline('grid-cols-{1..12}');
+/* paragraph--shortcut.html.twig: md:w-1/{{ min(loop.length, 3) }} lg:w-1/{{ min(loop.length, has_sidebar ? 3 : 6) }} */
+@source inline('{md:,lg:}w-1/{2,3,4,5,6}');

title: [RGDSD8-1249] feat(csp): add report-only Content-Security-Policy
description:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Tickets       | RGDSD8-1249
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | yes
| Deprecations? | no

Serve the policy in report-only mode first, so violations are observed
before enforcement is enabled.

Collect violations with the contrib reporting module and its reporting
endpoint, which records the fields we need. Route them to a rotating log
file (Monolog reporting channel) instead of the database, to avoid DB
pressure and bloat if violations spike.

Add scripts/csp-report.php, a local-only CLI to aggregate and triage that
log. It is deliberately not wired into the application.

Inject environment-dependent sources (Partoo proxy, micro_sso master
origin) at runtime through a POLICY_ALTER subscriber, since they cannot
be hardcoded in versioned config.

---

Wa can ask Claranet to add some guards like:

- `client_max_body_size` on `location ~ ^/system/reporting/`. A body cap enforced by nginx returns 413 before PHP boots. One caveat on sizing: application/reports+json repeats the full originalPolicy string in every report of a batch, so batches are larger than a naive per-report estimate.
- `limit_req` on the same location for rate limiting at the edge.
- Size-based `logrotate` on `app/logs/reporting/*.log` as the true hard disk bound (rotate at N MB, keep K, compress).

On nginx side something like:
```nginx
# http{} context: declares the zone, throttles nothing on its own
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=csp_report:10m rate=10r/s;

# server{} block, ordered before other regex locations
location ~ ^/system/reporting/ {
    client_max_body_size 64k;                 # recommended: caps bytes/request, returns 413
    limit_req zone=csp_report burst=50 nodelay;
    limit_req_status 429;
    try_files $uri /index.php?$query_string;   # should match their existing Drupal front-controller target
}
```

The logrotate config could look like:
```
/absolute/path/to/app/logs/reporting/*.log {
    size 50M
    rotate 20
    missingok
    notifempty
    compress
    delaycompress
    copytruncate
    su <web-user> <web-group>
}
```

Two correctness notes for ops: `copytruncate` is required because monolog does not reopen its logs on a signal, and this must run hourly (a cron.hourly drop-in or a timer), not the default daily, otherwise a fast flood fills the disk before logrotate ever checks the size. Monolog keeps owning the daily `*.log` naming and its 10-file prune; logrotate owns the compressed `*.gz` copies.

Do we need all of them? I don't know.  
Considering the potential attacks the sites are victims, having at least a little guard is interesting.

---

## TODO for deployment

- Add env variables `CSP_REPORT_ONLY=1` and `CSP_ENFORCE=0`
- ask claranet to remove CSP header from their side in production (val and dev done, see https://plume.fr.clara.net/tickets/ISS-100022708/projects/PRJ-4NIDT4)
- ask claranet to protect report endpoint

@@ -0,0 +1,218 @@ +# CSP violation reports + +The project ships a Content Security Policy (CSP) in report-only and/or enforce +mode. Browsers post every violation to an internal endpoint, which logs it. The +`scripts/csp-report.php` CLI parses those logs and aggregates them so you can +decide what to allow, what to fix, and what to ignore. + +Two facts stay out of this document because they change over time: + +- The active policy is defined in `config/sync/csp.settings.yml`. +- The authority for the policy in force when a given violation happened is the + report's own `originalPolicy` field, not the config. Runtime subscribers and + library declarations can add sources on top of the YAML, so the effective + policy and the configured base can differ. Read both before deciding whether a + violation is actionable. + +## Quick start + +```bash +# 1. Human summary of the top offenders +php scripts/csp-report.php app/logs/reporting/*.log* + +# 2. Machine-readable summary for scripts, CI, or an AI agent +php scripts/csp-report.php --mode=json app/logs/reporting/*.log* + +# 3. Rank actionable reports, dropping browser-extension noise +php scripts/csp-report.php --mode=tsv --fields=effectiveDirective,sourceFile app/logs/reporting/*.log* \ + | grep -Ev 'chrome-extension|moz-extension|safari-web-extension' \ + | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn +``` + +Run it with a plain PHP CLI (no Drupal bootstrap): locally inside the PHP +container (`make docker-shell-php`), on the server where the logs live. Run +`php scripts/csp-report.php --help` for the full list of modes, options, and +defaults. That help text is the reference; this guide is not. + +## Where the logs are + +Runtime logs are written under the Drupal web root at `app/logs/reporting/`, +rotated with one file per day (`reporting-handler-YYYY-MM-DD.log`). The +`app/logs/` tree is gitignored, so pull the files from the server before +analysing them. + +The parser reads plain and gzip (`*.gz`) files, several files or stdin at once, +and streams input line by line. Each line is one Monolog record carrying the +Reporting API payload as JSON inside `
...
`; the parser reads that +payload. Request metadata in the Monolog context (`ip`, `uid`, `user`) is not +aggregated: read the raw lines when you need to know who triggered a report. + +## Report fields that matter + +| Field | Meaning | How to use it | +|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------| +| `effectiveDirective` | Directive violated (`script-src-elem`, `style-src-attr`, ...). | Primary grouping key: the category of problem. | +| `blockedURL` | What was blocked: a URL, `inline`, or `eval`. | What resource is involved. | +| `disposition` | `report` (nothing blocked) or `enforce` (actually blocked). | Whether users are affected now. | +| `sourceFile` | File that triggered the violation. | Best signal for noise versus real. | +| `lineNumber`, `columnNumber` | Location in `sourceFile`. | Jump to the offending code. | +| `sample` | First ~40 chars of the inline content (only with `report-sample`). | Identify the exact snippet. | +| `documentURL` | Page where it happened. | Reproduce the violation. | +| `originalPolicy` | Full policy active at the time. | Authority for what was (dis)allowed. | + +The `-elem` versus `-attr` suffix decides the fix: + +- `script-src-elem`: a `

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+---
+2026/09/03
+
+---
+
+## Tailwind preset delivered by the frontend CI
+
+### Context
+
+The Tailwind design system (tokens, base styles, `btn--*` components) is owned by the ui-kit of the
+[frontend monorepo](https://gitlab.ekino.com/rgds/rgds-website-factory-frontend). With Tailwind 3,
+this repository installed the whole monorepo as a git npm dependency (`#master`, with a deploy token
+written in clear in `package.json`), copied `index.css` and `tailwind.config.js` in a `postinstall`
+script, and relied on a relative `require('./tailwind-purge')` inside the copied config to inject its
+own Twig/JS sources and safelist.
+
+Tailwind 4 moves the configuration to CSS (`preset.css` = `theme.css` + `base.css` +
+`components.css`, without any `@source`) and drops the JS `safelist`: the copy/`require` trick no
+longer works, and the git dependency had to be frozen and its token removed anyway.
+
+### Considered Options
+
+* Keep the git npm dependency, pinned on a SHA, with credentials injected from the environment
+  (`.env`, CI variable) through a git `insteadOf` configuration.
+* Have the existing `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the frontend repository copy the four preset
+  files into `app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/`, next to the SPA bundles it
+  already delivers, and drop the npm dependency.
+
+### Decision
+
+Chosen option: the preset is copied by the `drupal-bundles:update` job.
+
+`tailwind.css` (repository root) imports `tailwindcss`, then the local copy of `preset.css`, and
+declares the sources to scan. The ex-safelist becomes `@source inline(...)` directives.
+
+### Positive Consequences
+
+No secret in the repository, no SHA to maintain, no clone of the monorepo on each `yarn` install.
+SPA bundles and preset always come from the same frontend commit, so the classes used by the bundles
+are always known by the preset that compiles them.
+
+### Negative Consequences
+
+The preset files are duplicated in this repository and must never be edited here: any change goes
+through the frontend monorepo and a run of the `drupal-bundles:update` job.

@@ -0,0 +1,218 @@ +# CSP violation reports + +The project ships a Content Security Policy (CSP) in report-only and/or enforce +mode. Browsers post every violation to an internal endpoint, which logs it. The +`scripts/csp-report.php` CLI parses those logs and aggregates them so you can +decide what to allow, what to fix, and what to ignore. + +Two facts stay out of this document because they change over time: + +- The active policy is defined in `config/sync/csp.settings.yml`. +- The authority for the policy in force when a given violation happened is the + report's own `originalPolicy` field, not the config. Runtime subscribers and + library declarations can add sources on top of the YAML, so the effective + policy and the configured base can differ. Read both before deciding whether a + violation is actionable. + +## Quick start + +```bash +# 1. Human summary of the top offenders +php scripts/csp-report.php app/logs/reporting/*.log* + +# 2. Machine-readable summary for scripts, CI, or an AI agent +php scripts/csp-report.php --mode=json app/logs/reporting/*.log* + +# 3. Rank actionable reports, dropping browser-extension noise +php scripts/csp-report.php --mode=tsv --fields=effectiveDirective,sourceFile app/logs/reporting/*.log* \ + | grep -Ev 'chrome-extension|moz-extension|safari-web-extension' \ + | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn +``` + +Run it with a plain PHP CLI (no Drupal bootstrap): locally inside the PHP +container (`make docker-shell-php`), on the server where the logs live. Run +`php scripts/csp-report.php --help` for the full list of modes, options, and +defaults. That help text is the reference; this guide is not. + +## Where the logs are + +Runtime logs are written under the Drupal web root at `app/logs/reporting/`, +rotated with one file per day (`reporting-handler-YYYY-MM-DD.log`). The +`app/logs/` tree is gitignored, so pull the files from the server before +analysing them. + +The parser reads plain and gzip (`*.gz`) files, several files or stdin at once, +and streams input line by line. Each line is one Monolog record carrying the +Reporting API payload as JSON inside `
...
`; the parser reads that +payload. +### Handling PHPStan errors
+
+Every ignored error must be documented (`reportIgnoresWithoutComments: true`): explain if it is a false positive and why, or if it is real why it is not fixed, and what should be done (TODO).
+Ask yourself questions like: Is it a false positive? If yes why? If no why ignoring it? Is it a known issue? Should we contribute to something?
+
+- **False positive**: ignore it with a comment.
+- **Real error**: either fix it, or ignore it with a comment justifying why it is not fixed. If the same kind of error is already ignored in `phpstan.neon.dist`, add the new occurrence there too, to keep identical errors grouped together.
+
+Two ways to ignore, in order of preference:
+
+1. Inline, close to the code: `// @phpstan-ignore <identifier> (why it is ignored and what to do)`. For several errors on one line, give each identifier its own comment: `<id1> (reason), <id2> (reason)`. The parser is naive: do not put `,` or `()` inside a comment (write `getTimestamp` not `getTimestamp()`), otherwise the comment is not detected.
+2. Centralized in `phpstan.neon.dist` under `ignoreErrors`, with a preceding `#` comment. Use this when the same error repeats across files or is already grouped there.
+
+`phpstan-baseline.neon` is the legacy baseline: errors are unsorted and each entry is triage work. It must only shrink over time, by qualifying entries as false positives (move to a documented ignore) or by fixing them. Never regenerate it to hide new errors without asking the user its consent.

+  (design tokens, base styles, `btn--*` components...). **Do not edit it here**: it is copied, along
+  with the SPA bundles, by the `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the frontend repository.
+- To scan a new folder, add an `@source` directive to `tailwind.css`. Classes built dynamically in
+  Twig (e.g. `grid-cols-{{ count }}`) are not detected and must be listed with `@source inline(...)`.

+/*
+ * Tailwind CSS 4 entry point of the rgds_theme theme (built with `yarn build:stylesheet`).
+ *
+ * The ui-kit preset (design tokens, base styles, shared components) lives in
+ * app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/. It is a copy pushed by the
+ * `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the rgds-website-factory-frontend repository, along with the
+ * SPA bundles: do not edit it here, change it in the frontend monorepo instead.
+ *
+ * `@source` paths are relative to this file.
+ *
+ * Utilities are deliberately emitted OUTSIDE of the `utilities` cascade layer (the expanded form of
+ * `@import 'tailwindcss'`, without `layer(utilities)`): Drupal core, contrib modules and the theme
+ * component stylesheets are not layered, and a layered utility always loses against them whatever
+ * the source order or specificity (e.g. core `.hidden` would beat `md:block`, a theme rule would
+ * beat `flex` or `bg-white`). Unlayered utilities keep the Tailwind 3 cascade (order + specificity).
+ */
+@layer theme, base, components, utilities;
+@import 'tailwindcss/theme.css' layer(theme);
+@import 'tailwindcss/preflight.css' layer(base);
+@import 'tailwindcss/utilities.css' source(none);
+@import './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/preset.css';
+
+/* ===== SOURCES ===== */
+
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/templates';
+/* Includes the minified SPA bundles, whose classes must exist in this stylesheet. */
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/js';
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/templates';
+
+/* ===== DYNAMIC CLASSES (ex safelist) ===== */
+
+/* node--emergencies-page--full.html.twig: grid-cols-{{ node.field_chapters.value|length }} */

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+---
+2026/09/03
+
+---
+
+## Tailwind preset delivered by the frontend CI
+
+### Context
+
+The Tailwind design system (tokens, base styles, `btn--*` components) is owned by the ui-kit of the
+[frontend monorepo](https://gitlab.ekino.com/rgds/rgds-website-factory-frontend). With Tailwind 3,
+this repository installed the whole monorepo as a git npm dependency (`#master`, with a deploy token
+written in clear in `package.json`), copied `index.css` and `tailwind.config.js` in a `postinstall`
+script, and relied on a relative `require('./tailwind-purge')` inside the copied config to inject its
+own Twig/JS sources and safelist.
+
+Tailwind 4 moves the configuration to CSS (`preset.css` = `theme.css` + `base.css` +
+`components.css`, without any `@source`) and drops the JS `safelist`: the copy/`require` trick no
+longer works, and the git dependency had to be frozen and its token removed anyway.
+
+### Considered Options
+
+* Keep the git npm dependency, pinned on a SHA, with credentials injected from the environment
+  (`.env`, CI variable) through a git `insteadOf` configuration.
+* Have the existing `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the frontend repository copy the four preset
+  files into `app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/`, next to the SPA bundles it
+  already delivers, and drop the npm dependency.
+
+### Decision
+
+Chosen option: the preset is copied by the `drupal-bundles:update` job.
+
+`tailwind.css` (repository root) imports `tailwindcss`, then the local copy of `preset.css`, and
+declares the sources to scan. The ex-safelist becomes `@source inline(...)` directives.
+
+### Positive Consequences
+
+No secret in the repository, no SHA to maintain, no clone of the monorepo on each `yarn` install.
+SPA bundles and preset always come from the same frontend commit, so the classes used by the bundles
+are always known by the preset that compiles them.
+
+### Negative Consequences
+
+The preset files are duplicated in this repository and must never be edited here: any change goes
+through the frontend monorepo and a run of the `drupal-bundles:update` job.

@@ -0,0 +1,218 @@ +# CSP violation reports + +The project ships a Content Security Policy (CSP) in report-only and/or enforce +mode. Browsers post every violation to an internal endpoint, which logs it. The +`scripts/csp-report.php` CLI parses those logs and aggregates them so you can +decide what to allow, what to fix, and what to ignore. + +Two facts stay out of this document because they change over time: + +- The active policy is defined in `config/sync/csp.settings.yml`. +- The authority for the policy in force when a given violation happened is the + report's own `originalPolicy` field, not the config. Runtime subscribers and + library declarations can add sources on top of the YAML, so the effective + policy and the configured base can differ. Read both before deciding whether a + violation is actionable. + +## Quick start + +```bash +# 1. Human summary of the top offenders +php scripts/csp-report.php app/logs/reporting/*.log* + +# 2. Machine-readable summary for scripts, CI, or an AI agent +php scripts/csp-report.php --mode=json app/logs/reporting/*.log* + +# 3. Rank actionable reports, dropping browser-extension noise +php scripts/csp-report.php --mode=tsv --fields=effectiveDirective,sourceFile app/logs/reporting/*.log* \ + | grep -Ev 'chrome-extension|moz-extension|safari-web-extension' \ + | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn +``` + +Run it with a plain PHP CLI (no Drupal bootstrap): locally inside the PHP +container (`make docker-shell-php`), on the server where the logs live. Run +`php scripts/csp-report.php --help` for the full list of modes, options, and +defaults. That help text is the reference; this guide is not. + +## Where the logs are + +Runtime logs are written under the Drupal web root at `app/logs/reporting/`, +rotated with one file per day (`reporting-handler-YYYY-MM-DD.log`). The +`app/logs/` tree is gitignored, so pull the files from the server before +analysing them. + +The parser reads plain and gzip (`*.gz`) files, several files or stdin at once, +and streams input line by line. Each line is one Monolog record carrying the +Reporting API payload as JSON inside `
...
`; the parser reads that +payload. Request metadata in the Monolog context (`ip`, `uid`, `user`) is not +aggregated: read the raw lines when you need to know who triggered a report. + +## Report fields that matter + +| Field | Meaning | How to use it | +|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------| +| `effectiveDirective` | Directive violated (`script-src-elem`, `style-src-attr`, ...). | Primary grouping key: the category of problem. | +| `blockedURL` | What was blocked: a URL, `inline`, or `eval`. | What resource is involved. | +| `disposition` | `report` (nothing blocked) or `enforce` (actually blocked). | Whether users are affected now. | +| `sourceFile` | File that triggered the violation. | Best signal for noise versus real. | +| `lineNumber`, `columnNumber` | Location in `sourceFile`. | Jump to the offending code. | +| `sample` | First ~40 chars of the inline content (only with `report-sample`). | Identify the exact snippet. | +| `documentURL` | Page where it happened. | Reproduce the violation. | +| `originalPolicy` | Full policy active at the time. | Authority for what was (dis)allowed. | + +The `-elem` versus `-attr` suffix decides the fix: + +- `script-src-elem`: a `

+### Handling PHPStan errors
+
+Every ignored error must be documented (`reportIgnoresWithoutComments: true`): explain if it is a false positive and why, or if it is real why it is not fixed, and what should be done (TODO).
+Ask yourself questions like: Is it a false positive? If yes why? If no why ignoring it? Is it a known issue? Should we contribute to something?
+
+- **False positive**: ignore it with a comment.
+- **Real error**: either fix it, or ignore it with a comment justifying why it is not fixed. If the same kind of error is already ignored in `phpstan.neon.dist`, add the new occurrence there too, to keep identical errors grouped together.
+
+Two ways to ignore, in order of preference:
+
+1. Inline, close to the code: `// @phpstan-ignore <identifier> (why it is ignored and what to do)`. For several errors on one line, give each identifier its own comment: `<id1> (reason), <id2> (reason)`. The parser is naive: do not put `,` or `()` inside a comment (write `getTimestamp` not `getTimestamp()`), otherwise the comment is not detected.
+2. Centralized in `phpstan.neon.dist` under `ignoreErrors`, with a preceding `#` comment. Use this when the same error repeats across files or is already grouped there.
+
+`phpstan-baseline.neon` is the legacy baseline: errors are unsorted and each entry is triage work. It must only shrink over time, by qualifying entries as false positives (move to a documented ignore) or by fixing them. Never regenerate it to hide new errors without asking the user its consent.

+/*
+ * Tailwind CSS 4 entry point of the rgds_theme theme (built with `yarn build:stylesheet`).
+ *
+ * The ui-kit preset (design tokens, base styles, shared components) lives in
+ * app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/. It is a copy pushed by the
+ * `drupal-bundles:update` CI job of the rgds-website-factory-frontend repository, along with the
+ * SPA bundles: do not edit it here, change it in the frontend monorepo instead.
+ *
+ * `@source` paths are relative to this file.
+ *
+ * Utilities are deliberately emitted OUTSIDE of the `utilities` cascade layer (the expanded form of
+ * `@import 'tailwindcss'`, without `layer(utilities)`): Drupal core, contrib modules and the theme
+ * component stylesheets are not layered, and a layered utility always loses against them whatever
+ * the source order or specificity (e.g. core `.hidden` would beat `md:block`, a theme rule would
+ * beat `flex` or `bg-white`). Unlayered utilities keep the Tailwind 3 cascade (order + specificity).
+ */
+@layer theme, base, components, utilities;
+@import 'tailwindcss/theme.css' layer(theme);
+@import 'tailwindcss/preflight.css' layer(base);
+@import 'tailwindcss/utilities.css' source(none);
+@import './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/css/ui-kit/preset.css';
+
+/* ===== SOURCES ===== */
+
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/templates';
+/* Includes the minified SPA bundles, whose classes must exist in this stylesheet. */
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/themes/rgds_theme/assets/js';
+@source './app/profiles/rgds/modules/rgds_core/templates';
+
+/* ===== DYNAMIC CLASSES (ex safelist) ===== */
+
+/* node--emergencies-page--full.html.twig: grid-cols-{{ node.field_chapters.value|length }} */
+@source inline('grid-cols-{1..12}');
+/* paragraph--shortcut.html.twig: md:w-1/{{ min(loop.length, 3) }} lg:w-1/{{ min(loop.length, has_sidebar ? 3 : 6) }} */
+@source inline('{md:,lg:}w-1/{2,3,4,5,6}');

@@ -18,3 +18,17 @@ Danger only posts one comment and updates its content on subsequent
 Given this, it’s usually one of the first few comments
 in a merge request if not the first.
 If you didn’t see it, try to look from the start of the merge request.
+
+## Automatic AI review
+
+Danger posts a standalone merge request comment to ask `@reviewer` to review the changes.
+It posts the comment once, unless the merge request author is in
+`DANGER_AI_REVIEW_BLACKLIST` or the merge request has a `no danger` or `release`
+label.
+
+Set `DANGER_AI_REVIEW_BLACKLIST` to a comma separated list of GitLab user IDs,
+usernames, or both. Username comparisons are case insensitive. For example:
+
+```text
+42,another.user,108
+```
